jobs.title: Financial Analyst, Employee Benefits
jobs.jd: Come join our team! There are many reasons why EPIC Insurance Brokers & Consultants has become one of the fastest-growing firms in the insurance industry. Fueled and driven by capable, committed people who share common beliefs and values and “bring it” every day, EPIC is always looking for people who have “the right stuff” – people who know what they want and aren’t afraid to make it happen. Headquartered in New York City and founded in 2007, our company has over 4,000 employees nationwide. With locations spread out across the U.S., our local market knowledge and industry expertise helps support our clients' regional and global needs. We have grown very quickly since our founding, and we continue to see growth and success thanks to our hard-working and growth-minded employees. Our core values are: Owner mindset, Inspire trust, Think big, and Drive results. If these values and growth align with what you're looking for in your next career? Then consider joining our amazing team! LOCATION : This is a hybrid role for our Duluth, GA location. JOB OVERVIEW: Responsible for developing accurate and timely financial analysis for clients. Prepare various financial and quantitative analysis in support of Client Teams. Employ effective project management skills for balancing requests from multiple Client Teams and for the efficient delivery of results. Requires effective communication skills for clearly explaining detailed analysis to Client Teams and Clients, and the ability to understand Client Teams/Client perspectives that can be reflected in the development of deliverables. WHAT YOU’LL DO: Support Employee Benefit Account Teams • Develop and review monthly reporting for assigned clients • Prepare IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) analysis • Produce underwriting analysis for client renewals and projections • Produce data warehouse-based reports to support plan performance analysis for clients • Support Client Team strategy initiatives with evaluation of plan design alternatives, rate or employee contribution alternatives, risk profiles, benchmarking, data analytics, vendor change analyses, or program implementation or elimination (financial or quantifiable impact) • Coordinate with vendors as needed to obtain necessary data for analysis New Business Development • Participate in new business activities and meetings as requested WHAT YOU’LL BRING: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent educational training or business experience • College degree in insurance, risk management, math or related field preferred • Aptitude for performing financial analysis for a benefits consulting or brokerage firm (we will provide training). KSAs (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities) • Microsoft Office Suite experience including large data sets • Able to effectively interface with internal and external customers • Able to handle confidential information with maximum discretion • Able to understand business principles and apply them accordingly • Able to work independently and on a team within a fast-paced, deadline driven environment • Career-focused • Demonstrate good judgment while managing projects, multi-tasking, prioritizing, and meeting deadlines with a sense of urgency • Detail-oriented, organized, efficient, and proactive • Excellent written/verbal communication skills including communicating complex financial information • High level of accountability and flexibility • High-touch client orientation • Open and willing to receive and give constructive critique • Strong analytical and quantitative skills Special Requirements • Flexible to work outside normal working hours COMPENSATION: Compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, training, certifications, education, internal equity, and market data. This role may also be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package. WHY EPIC: EPIC has over 60 offices and 4,000 employees nationwide – and we’re growing! It’s a great time to join the team and be a part of this growth. We offer: Generous Paid Time off Managed PTO for salaried/exempt employees (personal time off without accruals or caps); 22 PTO days starting out for hourly/non-exempt employees; 12 company-observed paid holidays; 4 early-close days Generous leave time options: Paid parental leave, pregnancy disability and bonding leave, and organ donor/bone marrow donor leave Generous employee referral bonus program of $1,500 per hired referral Employee recognition programs for demonstrating EPIC’s values plus additional employee recognition awards and programs (and trips!) Employee Resource Groups: Women’s Coalition, EPIC Veterans Group Professional growth & development: Mentorship Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Leadership Development Unique benefits such as Pet Insurance, Identity Theft & Fraud Protection Coverage, Legal Planning, Family Planning, and Menopause & Midlife Support Additional benefits include (but are not limited to): 401(k) matching, medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, and wellness & employee assistance programs 50/50 Work Culture: EPIC fosters a 50/50 culture between producers and the rest of the business, supporting collaboration, teamwork, and an inclusive work environment. It takes both production and service to be EPIC! EPIC Gives Back – Some of our charitable efforts include Donation Connection, Employee Assistance Fund, and People First Foundation We’re in the top 10 of property/casualty agencies according to “Insurance Journal” To learn more about EPIC, visit our Careers Page: https://www.epicbrokers.com/about/epic-careers/ . EPIC embraces diversity in all its various forms—whether it be diversity of thought, background, race, religion, gender, skills or experience. We are committed to fostering a work community where every colleague feels welcomed, valued, respected and heard. It is our belief that diversity drives innovation and that creating an environment where every employee feels included and empowered, helps us to deliver the best outcome to our clients. California Applicants - View your privacy rights at: https://www.epicbrokers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/epic-ca-employee-privacy-notice.pdf . jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.jd:
Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. 

We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024. We're now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.



Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Data Science team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - AI & Automation

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.



Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 



What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Data Science & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

 

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

 
 

While we appreciate your interest and application, due to the volume of applications we receive, only applicants under consideration will be contacted.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - Credit (Retros)
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


ABOUT THE TEAM

We’re part of Plaid’s Data organization, building models and insights that help millions of people better understand and grow their financial lives. We use Plaid’s unique financial data to help lenders make more informed decisions and build better credit experiences.

We partner across data science, engineering, product, and Go-to-Market to turn complex data into practical customer recommendations and scalable solutions. We value technical rigor, creativity, user empathy, and teamwork.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on the Credit team, you’ll apply quantitative analysis and deep credit expertise to help lenders make better use of cash flow insights. You’ll work across customer problems, credit policy, and data products—translating Plaid’s data into recommendations and insights that drive business impact and inform product direction.

Your day-to-day responsibilities may include:

 - Deep-dive into model performance for clients, triage issues, and identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

 - Analyze Plaid’s unique data to identify emerging credit risk signals and build and evaluate credit retrospectives.

 - Create tailored recommendations for clients based on their data and Plaid’s insights.

 - Build and maintain data pipelines, including ETL processes using tools such as dbt.

 - Develop metrics, alerts, and dashboards to monitor production machine learning model performance.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the process of developing hands-on recommendations for incorporating cash flow insights into lending decisions, using best practices for account-level decisioning.

 - Improve customer adoption of Plaid Insights through custom analysis tailored to each customer’s needs.

 - Serve as a subject matter expert on credit insights and credit policy implementation, supporting Data Science, Engineering, and Go-to-Market partners.

 - Apply your expertise in quantitative analysis, data mining, and data visualization to develop models and actionable insights.

 - Identify useful signals that can inform machine learning models.

 - Inform and influence Product and Engineering teams through clear analysis and presentations.



WHAT EXCITES YOU

 - Applying data science and credit expertise to real-world lending decisions.

 - Working with Plaid’s unique financial data to uncover emerging credit risk signals and create useful customer insights.

 - Helping lenders make more informed decisions with cash flow data and account-level recommendations.

 - Partnering across Data Science, Engineering, Product, and Go-to-Market to turn analysis into customer and product impact.

 - Working on high-impact problems that can improve financial access and outcomes.



WHAT EXCITES US

 - 2–5 years of industry experience in a financial services Data Science role.

 - Deep familiarity with SQL and Python.

 - Deep understanding of credit risk and the development of underwriting models.

 - Hands-on credit expertise building and maintaining credit policies for lenders.

 - Knowledge of the lending lifecycle and how to optimize each step, including marketing, acquisition, customer management, and collections or recoveries.

 - Demonstrated ability to make data-driven decisions.

 - Nice to have: Experience building data pipelines and automating ETL processes with dbt or similar tools.

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!



Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Plaid is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance with your application or interviews due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@plaid.com.



Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice here https://plaid.com/legal/#candidate-privacy-notice.


Additional compensation in the form(s) of equity and/or commission are dependent on the position offered. Plaid provides a comprehensive benefit plan, including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k). Pay is based on factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience and skillset, and location. Pay and benefits are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefit plans.

jobs.title: Quant Risk Analyst - Derivatives & Clearing
jobs.jd:
ABOUT POLYMARKET

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets.

This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization.

 - Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation.

 - Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests.

 - Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations.

 - Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment.

 - Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly.

 - Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture.

 - Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar.

 - Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes.

 - Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts.

 - Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context.

 - Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong.

 - Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices).

 - Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience.

 - Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra.


NICE TO HAVE

 - C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems.

 - Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets.

 - Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology).

 - Experience building real-time risk systems.


PAY TRANSPARENCY

Base salary range: $400,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.


LOCATION & WORK SETUP

This role is based in our New York City office, in person. You'll be working directly alongside the trading, engineering, and risk teams.

jobs.title: Graduate Analyst
jobs.jd: Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money. Min fees. Max ease. Full speed. Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money. As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money. For everyone, everywhere. More about our mission and what we offer . As a Graduate Product Analyst, you’ll join our North America Regional Analytics team in September 2027. This full-time role is a chance to make a real impact early and kickstart your career. You’ll be onboarded with the global Graduate cohort in one of our offices and learn the basics of being a Wiser. The Role: We’re hiring three graduates to work as analysts inside our North America product teams, which build Wise for personal and business customers in the US and Canada. Our analysts don’t sit in a central reporting team: each one works day to day with product managers & engineers and helps them decide what to build next and whether it worked. You’ll join one of four teams: Onboarding, Send, Account or Growth. Each owns a different stage of the customer’s journey with Wise, and each is described below. You won’t be on your own. A senior analyst will mentor you, review your work and help you grow, and you’ll be part of a team of analysts covering the whole North America product. What you’ll be doing: Shape Strategy & Prioritization: You’ll help your team understand where customers struggle and what is worth fixing first. That means digging into funnels and customer behavior, reading customer feedback and survey responses, and sizing opportunities so the team can prioritize the work with the biggest impact. As you grow, you’ll lead your own discoveries and present recommendations to your product manager. Learn Launch Rigor & Experimentation: You’ll help design and analyze A/B tests and pre/post comparisons for new features, and learn to turn the results into a clear call: roll out, iterate or roll back. You’ll keep an eye on your team’s core metrics and flag when something looks wrong. Build on the Semantic Layer: We believe analysts add the most value when they focus on product discovery, not ad-hoc requests. You’ll learn to build and maintain the data models and dashboards that let your team answer their own questions, using Snowflake, dbt, Git, Airflow, Python and Lightdash, and help improve the AI skills that run our routine reporting. Share What You Learn: You’ll explain your findings to your team and the wider NorthAm squad, in writing, in charts and in person, so that your work leads to a decision. How we work with AI: We lean hard into AI: AI skills produce our routine work and deep dives, so our analysts can focus on discovery. You’ll use AI tools every day, and you’ll own the answer, not the tool: checking the data, the logic and the conclusion before anyone acts on it. Where you could join: Onboarding Onboarding owns the first steps of a customer’s journey: creating a profile, getting verified (Know Your Customer / Know Your Business checks) and taking a first action with Wise. It also keeps financial crime out at the front door. The core challenge is letting genuine customers through quickly while stopping bad actors. You might work on questions like: Where do new customers drop out between signing up and their first transfer, and what would bring them back? Which verification steps slow genuine customers down without catching more fraud or financial crime? Send Send covers what happens when a customer sends money, and is made up of three teams: Pay-in: how customers pay money into Wise, for example by bank transfer (ACH) or card. Which payment methods help customers complete their transfer, and what does each one cost us? Payout: how money reaches recipients’ bank accounts in the US and Canada, balancing three levers: cost, speed and conversion. What would make these payouts faster or cheaper, and how much more volume would that bring? You’ll also help track the health of our banking partners. Payment Risk: transfer suspensions and ACH and card chargebacks. How do we cut losses from chargebacks and fraud without blocking good customers? Account Account owns how customers use Wise as an account, not only for one-off transfers: getting paid into Wise with USD and CAD local account details, spending with the Wise debit card, and earning a return on money held with Wise. You might work on questions like: What makes a customer start getting paid into their Wise account, and what makes them keep doing it? Who uses the Wise card, for what, and what stops others from using it? Does holding money with Wise change how customers send money abroad? Growth Growth owns the top of the funnel: how people find Wise and decide to try it. That covers landing pages, the promotion engine, corridor strategy (which country-to-country routes we focus on) and pricing, where you’ll work with our Pricing Data Science team to understand how price affects demand. You might work on questions like: Did a promotion bring in customers who stay, or customers who leave once it ends? Which corridors should we focus on next, and why? Your first six months: By three months: you own part of your team’s regular metrics and have delivered your first analysis. By six months: you’ve led a discovery or an experiment readout from question to recommendation and presented it to your team. Qualifications What you’ll bring: Education: A bachelor’s or master’s degree in a quantitative field such as economics, statistics, mathematics, computer science or engineering, completed by your start date, or equivalent practical experience. Technical Foundations: You’ve used SQL, Python or R to answer a real question with data, in a course, a project, an internship or on your own. You understand the basics of statistics, such as distributions, hypothesis tests and confidence intervals, and can tell when a difference is real rather than noise. Curiosity & Product Sense: You want to know why customers behave the way they do, and you ask “so what should we do?” about every result. Clear Communication: You can explain a finding to someone who isn’t technical, in writing and in conversation, and you’re comfortable saying “I don’t know yet”. Ownership: You finish what you start, ask for help early and act on feedback. AI with Judgment: You use AI tools to work faster, and you check their output before you trust it. Right to Work: You must be authorized to work in the US. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Nice to have but not essential: Hands-on experience with any of Snowflake, dbt, Git, Airflow or Lightdash. Exposure to A/B testing or causal inference, in a course or in practice. An internship or project in analytics, data science, product or finance. An interest in payments, fintech, or how people move and manage money across borders. For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive. We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences. Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers. If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs . Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram .

jobs.jd: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About the Role: The mission of the Falcon Intel Recon Analyst is to directly support cyber threat customers and to ensure our customers realize the full value of the Intelligence product they have purchased from CrowdStrike; ultimately maximizing customer success and renewals. Analysts are responsible for working with multiple customers to manage the customer's Falcon Intel Recon module. This role will serve as a cyber intel analytic interface between CrowdStrike's Falcon Intelligence Recon customers and the wider CrowdStrike intelligence team, enabling effective use of cyber threat intelligence between clients and the Falcon Intel Recon application. Ideal candidates possess working knowledge of dark web intelligence and threat intelligence, complemented by customer engagement skills across technical and executive levels. You should demonstrate the ability to independently manage multiple concurrent workstreams and have a genuine passion for delivering outstanding customer experiences. The role requires understanding and addressing customer needs at all organizational levels, from C-suite executives to security analysts. This role requires PST working hours. What You'll Do: Drive high levels of customer satisfaction, maintaining a strong sense of ownership over many customer relationships. Quickly triage and escalate noteworthy findings from Falcon Intelligence Recon to the respective customers Guide customers through Falcon Intelligence Recon findings and providing subject matter expertise Be a strong voice for customers into the Intelligence and Engineering teams to improve the product and ensure that customer's feedback, feature requests, and overall satisfaction is conveyed and accounted for Travel: Minimal to light travel (5%) What You'll Need: Working knowledge of cyber threat intelligence, all-source threat intelligence analysis, or intelligence collections and be fully versed in the intelligence lifecycle Good written, verbal communication skills in English Working knowledge of cyber threat intelligence terminology, key concepts, and analysis Basic understanding of the dark and deep web ecosystems, including actors, forums, and leak sites Adaptable and willing to learn new technologies Customer service attitude and willingness to help and problem-solve with customers Ability to operate independently and with little direction. Ability to present and explain technology to people with less technical knowledge Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Must be able to thrive in a fast paced, high stress start up environment and able to create customer solutions with limited resources Knowledge of data communication concepts and technologies, specifically email, networking, and enterprise security Bonus Points: Ability to use AI tools and familiarity with application programming interfaces (API) as a delivery method for indicators and intelligence. Curiosity about how AI, machine learning, and autonomous agents can enhance darkweb analysis, intelligence analysis, and customer outcomes #LI-AM1 Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike: Market leader in compensation and equity awards Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge Paid parental and adoption leaves Professional development opportunities for all employees regardless of level or role Employee Networks, geographic neighborhood groups, and volunteer opportunities to build connections Vibrant office culture with world class amenities Great Place to Work Certified™ across the globe CrowdStrike is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Compensation Analyst
jobs.jd: We are looking for a creative, data-driven Compensation Analyst to join our team. If you are a problem solver with strong analytical prowess, excellent communication skills, and a genuine passion for data analytics, this role is for you. As a Compensation Analyst, you won’t just crunch numbers—you will contribute to the strategic development and implementation of our compensation programs. You will collaborate with team members to develop modern analytic tools, automate legacy processes, and help compose the future of our compensation strategy. The ideal candidate is enthusiastic, hardworking, and thrives on building elegant analytical models. What You’ll Be Doing: Evolve Compensation Strategy: Help us redefine and evolve how we believe about base, variable, and equity compensation structures. Advanced Analytics: Apply quantitative and qualitative analysis to identify problems, develop hypotheses, and recommend data-backed solutions for compensation programs and processes. Data Visualization & Modeling: Build and develop dynamic dashboards and analytic models to provide actionable business insights and interpret market or internal trends. Workday Optimization: Partner with the HRIS/Systems team to implement, test, and define requirements for Workday performance and compensation modules, ensuring seamless updates to structures and job profiles. Drive Automation: Streamline and automate monthly, quarterly, and annual compensation reporting and analysis using modern data tools and AI workflows. Market Benchmarking: Conduct global market benchmarking, assess peer groups, and ensure consistent market pricing practices while maintaining internal equity. Storytelling with Data: Provide sophisticated compensation analytics, clearly conveying complex findings and recommendations to collaborators. What We Need to See: BA/BS degree, preferably in a quantitative-focused major (e.g., Finance, Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics) or equivalent experience. 5+ years of dedicated, progressive experience in Compensation. Core Tech Stack: Advanced proficiency in Excel (complex formulas, VBA, Power Query) and a strong working knowledge of HRIS systems (preferably Workday). Communication: Outstanding written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable narratives. Soft Skills: High learning agility, flexibility, and unmatched quantitative problem-solving skills. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: AI & Automation Savvy: Experience bringing to bear AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Advanced Data Analysis, Microsoft Copilot) to accelerate data cleaning, script writing, and compensation reporting. BI & Visualization: Proven experience building interactive dashboards using Tableau, Power BI, or other advanced analytic platforms. Coding & Automation: Familiarity with Python, R, or SQL for data manipulation and automating repetitive workflows. Project Mastery: Strong planning, organizational, and project management skills with a track record of driving initiatives from concept to completion. Scalable Processes: Demonstrated experience developing and implementing scalable, repeatable processes backed by detailed ongoing documentation. Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/ Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are: 112,000 USD – 178,250 USD for Level 3; and 144,000 USD – 230,000 USD for Level 4. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits . jobs.title: Configuration Analyst II
jobs.jd: Founded in 1977 as the Senior Care Action Network, SCAN began with a simple but radical idea: that older adults deserve to stay healthy and independent. That belief was championed by a group of community activists we still honor today as the “12 Angry Seniors.” Their mission continues to guide everything we do. Today, SCAN is a nonprofit health organization serving more than 500,000 people across Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas, and Washington, with over $8 billion in annual revenue. With nearly five decades of experience, we have built a distinctive, values-driven platform dedicated to improving care for older adults. Our work spans Medicare Advantage, fully integrated care models, primary care, care for the most medically and socially complex populations, and next-generation care delivery models. Across all of this, we are united by a shared commitment: combining compassion with discipline, innovation with stewardship, and growth with integrity. At SCAN, we believe scale should strengthen—not dilute—our mission. We are building the future of care for older adults, grounded in purpose, accountability, and respect for the people and communities we serve. The Job The Configuration Analyst II supports implementation, maintenance, and governance of SCAN Health Plan’s Benefit Configuration, including Prior Authorization (PA) and Pre-Determination (PD) code sets. This role ensures approved code sets are accurately and timely configured across claims, utilization management, and related operational systems. Supports benefit configuration and prior authorization activities, including configuration, testing, validation, deployment, and post implementation review. Familiarity with healthcare vendor platforms such as MHK, ikaSystems, CareAxis, or similar applications. Experience utilizing AI-enabled analytical tools and automation technologies. Coursework or training in healthcare analytics, healthcare informatics, business intelligence, or database management. Certification or coursework in SQL and Power BI. This role reports to Director of Data Science and Analytics. This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week. These tasks will include –among others- the development of predictive models and business intelligence solutions of moderate scope and complexity for customers within the various industries served by TransUnion. The team develops risk based data-driven insights, monitors emerging risk and regulatory developments, supports peer and industry benchmarking, and strengthens independent risk oversight through high-quality analytics and reporting. We are seeking a detail-oriented Data Analyst with strong technical, analytical, and communication skills who can translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for risk partners and senior management. Basic Qualifications - Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience - Typically more than five years of applicable experience Preferred Skills/Experience · Bachelor’s degree or higher in Data Analytics, Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field. · Three or more years of experience in data analytics, financial risk management, banking, financial services, or a related field; equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered. · Proficiency in SQL and advanced spreadsheet analysis; experience with Python, R, or a comparable analytical programming language is preferred. · Experience with data visualization and business intelligence tools, such as Power BI or Tableau, and with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and PowerPoint. · Strong ability to work with large or complex datasets, reconcile information across sources, identify data-quality issues, and document analytical logic and results. · Understanding of banking, financial markets, balance-sheet management, or financial risk concepts, including liquidity, interest rate, capital, or market risk, is preferred. · Familiarity with applicable banking laws, regulations, regulatory reporting, and risk-management expectations is a plus. · Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and project-management skills, with close attention to detail and accuracy. · Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain technical findings to non-technical audiences. · Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, collaborate across functions, and deliver high-quality work within established timelines. · Demonstrated intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and a commitment to effective challenge, continuous improvement, and high standards of data integrity. jobs.title: Public Health Data Analyst
jobs.jd: We are seeking a Public Health Data Analyst to support data analysis, data quality, visualization, and epidemiologic activities for public health surveillance programs. This position combines hands-on quantitative analysis with an understanding of epidemiology, surveillance systems, and public health data. The ideal candidate will bring a strong foundation in either public health surveillance, including syndromic surveillance and ESSENCE, or analytical programming and data analysis using R or comparable tools. This role offers the opportunity to apply those skills to meaningful public health surveillance work while developing additional expertise and working closely with project colleagues and clients. Key Responsibilities Monitor and analyze public health surveillance data using ESSENCE, R, and other analytical tools to identify trends, patterns, anomalies, data-quality issues, and potential public health events of interest. Support enhanced and time-sensitive surveillance activities, including analysis, reporting, and development or maintenance of analytical and dashboard products using CDC-provided formats and requirements. Contribute to reports, slides, dashboards, and other analytical products for CDC and response partners, working with senior epidemiologists and analysts as appropriate. Support the development, testing, and validation of syndrome definitions and surveillance categories, incorporating feedback from CDC subject-matter experts and STLT public health partners. Support analysis and reporting of emergency department data and additional public health data sources, such as NNDSS, commercial laboratory, Veteran’s Affairs, and other data sources, as they are incorporated into surveillance activities. Take ownership of assigned analytical work, manage multiple priorities and short timelines, and communicate questions, issues, or risks as they arise. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Data Science, Informatics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field and 2-4 years of relevant professional experience in public health, epidemiology, healthcare data analysis, surveillance, or a related analytical field. 3+ years experience with either public health or syndromic surveillance, including ESSENCE or comparable surveillance systems; or 3+ years experience with analytical programming and data analysis using R, or comparable tools. Experience analyzing public health, epidemiologic, healthcare, or other complex datasets. Ability to take ownership of assigned work, manage competing priorities, and communicate questions or issues as they arise. Understanding of basic epidemiologic and statistical concepts. Experience cleaning, transforming, validating, analyzing, or visualizing data. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and documentation skills. Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Preferred Qualifications Experience with syndromic surveillance and/or ESSENCE. Experience using R or other analytical programming tools for public health or epidemiologic analysis. Experience working with state, local, tribal, or territorial (STLT) public health agencies or their surveillance data, systems, or reporting activities. Master's degree in Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Data Science, Informatics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field. Familiarity with healthcare and public health data standards or terminology, such as HL7, ICD-9/10, SNOMED, or LOINC. Working at ICF ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. jobs.title: Economist, Macro & Economic Insights
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.



The Economics Team uses economic research and data science to deepen our understanding of economic, credit, and financial trends. We combine rigorous empirical analysis with clear communication to inform decisions across and beyond Plaid.



You will conduct applied economic research, develop reliable analytical methods, and turn complex findings into clear, useful insights. Working with economists and data scientists, you will own research projects from question framing and data preparation through validation and written communication. This is a hands-on role for an economist who enjoys working with large datasets, exercising sound judgment, and explaining evidence and limitations to a range of audiences. You will have opportunities to develop a research specialty and take on broader ownership as the team grows.



We're guided by our principles including impact, growing together, embracing openness and positivity, and inventing tomorrow; we're looking for leaders who are motivated by those same principles






Responsibilities

 - Investigating economic questions and trends through rigorous empirical research, from framing the question through analysis, validation, and communication

 - Working with large, complex datasets to develop reliable measures and reproducible analytical workflows

 - Evaluating findings against established research and public benchmarks, assessing data quality and representativeness, and clearly communicating uncertainty and limitations

 - Applying econometric and time-series methods to test hypotheses, assess robustness, and distinguish meaningful patterns from noise

 - Writing clear research briefs and presenting findings to technical and nontechnical audiences; partnering with colleagues across research, data science, and the business to identify useful questions and inform decisions






Qualifications

 - PhD in economics or a related empirical field, or a Master's plus 4+ years of relevant applied experience, with strong empirical training. Exceptional candidates completing their PhD in 2027 are welcome; relevant research includes applied macroeconomics, household or behavioral finance, fintech, and financial regulation

 - Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience independently analyzing large, complex datasets and building reproducible analytical workflows

 - Strong econometric and time-series modeling skills, with experience applying these methods to economic questions and assessing robustness

 - Excellent writing for non-academic audiences, demonstrated through policy memos, market commentary, or research briefs. You can explain and defend your methods, findings, and limitations to technical and nontechnical audiences

 - Sound research judgment: you distinguish evidence from interpretation, communicate uncertainty, and scope claims to what the data supports

 - Nice to have: experience conducting applied economic research in fintech, finance, a research institute, or a public-sector organization; prior ownership of a recurring research publication

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!



Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Plaid is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance with your application or interviews due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@plaid.com.



Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice here https://plaid.com/legal/#candidate-privacy-notice.

jobs.title: Revenue Strategy & Operations
jobs.jd:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re looking for someone to join our team in Revenue Strategy & Operations and play a key role in scaling our go-to-market operations. This role is at the intersection of technical problem-solving and operational excellence, focusing on building and maintaining tools, automations, and dashboards that empower our sales, data, and product teams to execute with precision.

As part of the Revenue Operations team, you'll collaborate across functions to design and implement systems that streamline sales processes, enhance decision-making, and drive growth. jobs.jd:

Reporting to the Sr. Director of AI & Analytics within our centralized Operations organization, this is a highly hands-on role focused on architecting scalable analytics systems and AI-enabled workflows that power decision-making across the company.

You will design the core data models, architecture, and reusable assets that serve Product, Engineering & Design — while helping redefine what an analytics function looks like in the age of AI.

This is a foundational hire with high ownership and long-term growth potential.

1. Enterprise Data Modeling & Architecture

 - Design and maintain scalable dbt data models in Snowflake that serve as trusted sources of truth across the business

 - Architect data pipelines and transformation workflows using Fivetran and modern ELT practices

 - Develop durable, extensible data assets that evolve as the company scales

 - Establish modeling standards, documentation practices, and governance frameworks

 - Partner with RevOps and Finance to define and operationalize core SaaS metrics (ARR, retention, expansion, pipeline, etc.)
   

2. AI-Enabled Systems & Workflow Integration

 - Build data foundations that power internal AI applications and LLM-enabled workflows

 - Prototype and productionize AI-driven operational use cases

 - Integrate analytics and AI into everyday workflows using tools such as Notion, Cursor, Glean, and other emerging platforms

 - Design systems that embed data directly into operational processes — not just dashboards
   

3. Cross-Functional Analytics Infrastructure

 - Partner with leaders across Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Engineering to translate business needs into scalable technical systems

 - Create reusable data assets that enable activation via Hightouch and analysis via Omni

 - Ensure architecture is scalable, secure, and adaptable to evolving enterprise requirements
   

Our Stack

Analytics: Fivetran, dbt, Snowflake, Hightouch, Omni
AI & Knowledge Systems: Notion, Cursor, Glean

Experience with these tools is helpful but not required. Strong fundamentals and the ability to quickly learn new technologies matter more than prior tool exposure.

 - 3-6 years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or similar hands-on roles

 - Strong SQL skills and deep understanding of modern data modeling (dimensional modeling, transformations, data contracts, etc.)

 - Experience building in cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, etc.)

 - Comfort working in a fast-moving, evolving AI tooling landscape

 - Systems-level thinker who designs for scalability, extensibility, and flexibility

 - Naturally curious and energized by solving ambiguous problems

 - Pride in building clean, durable architecture — not just shipping quick fixes

 - Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across business and technical teams

 - Nice to have: Experience with Pendo, Amplitude, Heap, or Mixpanel



Why This Role Matters

We are not building a traditional BI function.

We are building an AI-augmented analytics capability that:

 - Embeds data into operational workflows

 - Enables faster, smarter enterprise decision-making

 - Evolves as AI tooling evolves

 - Treats architecture as a strategic asset, not a back-office utility
   

You won’t just build dashboards — you will help shape how analytics and AI power our company over the next several years.

The University of Miami’s Business School has an exciting opportunity for a full-time Data Analyst 3 to work on the Coral Gables campus. Job Description Title: Data Analyst III Department: Department of Health Management and Policy, University of Miami Business School Reports to Dr. Michael T. French, Professor and Chair of the Department of Health Management and Policy Location: Coral Gables, FL (in-person) Training: A master’s or doctorate degree in economics, public policy, health policy, health services research, or a closely related field with graduate training in econometrics, completed by the start date Start date: As soon as possible, ideally by December 2026 and no later than January 2027 Job Summary The Data Analyst III will conduct applied empirical research in health economics, health services research, and health policy alongside research-active faculty in the Department of Health Management and Policy (HMP) at the University of Miami Business School. The work is primarily quantitative and spans the full research process: developing research questions and identification strategies, cleaning and analyzing data, implementing causal inference methods, producing tables and figures, and drafting sections of manuscripts for peer-reviewed journals and conference presentations. We are seeking a candidate with strong training in econometrics and a genuine interest in academic research. Candidates should have experience implementing causal inference methods (e.g., difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity) with a solid understanding of endogeneity and causal identification. Applicants whose training is primarily in data analytics, business analytics, or data science, without complementary graduate coursework in econometrics, are unlikely to be a good fit. Beyond the requisite technical skills, the ideal candidate will bring professional maturity: the ability to take initiative, communicate proactively, exercise sound judgment with limited oversight, and contribute intellectually to the direction of the research. This is a full-time research support position. The Data Analyst’s time is dedicated to faculty-led projects, with no protected time for independent research. Co-authorship opportunities on resulting manuscripts are at the discretion of the lead faculty member and are based on substantive intellectual contribution. The role is best suited to master’s- or PhD-trained candidates seeking a sustained career in applied research as part of a faculty-led team. It is not a post-doctoral position, and candidates focused on building an independent research agenda are unlikely to find it a good fit. To apply, please submit (1) a resume or CV, (2) unofficial graduate transcripts, (3) a list of three references with contact information, and (4) a cover letter of no more than two pages. The cover letter should describe your background and fit for the role, your interest in being based in Miami, and one causal inference analysis or similar project you have implemented, including the research question, the econometric method(s), and the statistical software program used. Job Responsibilities Explore new datasets and propose potential research questions and identification strategies to faculty. Contribute to study design and protocol development, including discussions of causal identification strategies, data requirements, and advanced analytic approaches. Clean, manage, and analyze research datasets with limited direction, maintaining reproducible, well-documented code. Draft tables, figures, methods sections, and other components of manuscripts, conference abstracts, posters, and internal memos. Summarize data and preliminary findings for faculty and research teams. Conduct literature reviews to inform study design and manuscript framing. Communicate proactively and professionally with faculty and research teams, including timely responses to correspondence and clear escalation when issues arise. Serve as project coordinator for data contracts the department has entered into with public and private organizations. Prepare and maintain IRB protocols and related correspondence for projects involving primary data collection. Other duties as assigned. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required: A master’s or doctorate degree in economics, public policy, health policy, health services research, or a closely related field, completed by the start date. Graduate coursework in econometrics and hands-on experience applying causal inference methods (e.g., difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity). Strong proficiency in Stata (preferred) and/or R for econometric analysis. Demonstrated interest in academic research in health economics, health services research, health policy, or a related field, and prior experience producing research deliverables (e.g., tables and figures, manuscript sections). Strong critical thinking skills and a willingness to problem-solve proactively and independently rather than wait for direction. Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines with limited supervision. Excellent organizational, written, and oral communication skills, and strong attention to detail. Preferred but not required: Experience with Git/GitHub for version control and collaborative project management. Experience with LaTeX for academic writing. Familiarity with SQL, cloud computing, or text analysis. Interest in using AI-assisted programming tools (LLM-based coding agents) to augment and accelerate research projects. Familiarity with IRB processes and regulatory requirements for human subjects research. Turn complex data into clear insights that help leaders act with confidence. As a Data Measurement & Reporting Advisor supporting Data Management & Reporting within DS&I, you will build trusted analytics, solve challenging data questions, and shape decisions that improve operational performance. You will join a team of ambitious, compassionate experts who value curiosity, partnership, and continuous growth. Responsibilities Design standardized performance analytics that align DS&I priorities with enterprise goals and guide timely decisions. Build measurement frameworks, data definitions, and methods that improve the consistency and trustworthiness of reporting. Develop and automate Tableau dashboards that turn complex data into clear insights and recommended actions. Partner with business leaders to define key questions, translate needs into analytical solutions, and measure results. Evaluate trends, risks, opportunities, and performance drivers through root-cause, variance, and operational analysis. Use advanced SQL to validate results, investigate data issues, and analyze information across multiple sources. Apply SAS, Altair, or Python to prepare data, automate work, and solve complex analytical problems. Resolve reporting, data quality, and measurement issues in partnership with IT and cross-functional teams. Deliver executive-ready reporting that highlights results, risks, business impact, and practical next steps. Create reusable templates and clear documentation that strengthen quality, accuracy, and team capabilities. Manage priorities independently while meeting commitments and building trusted stakeholder relationships. Qualifications 5+ years of hands-on experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or another data-focused field. Advanced Tableau experience required , including personally designing and developing dashboards and visual analytics solutions. Advanced SQL skills required , including complex queries, data validation, troubleshooting, and analysis across multiple data sources. Experience using SAS, Altair, or Python required for analytics, data preparation, automation, or complex problem-solving. Experience designing operational KPIs, performance reports, dashboards, and analytics solutions. Demonstrated success investigating data, reporting, and measurement issues and driving them to resolution. Ability to perform root-cause, trend, and variance analysis and turn findings into business recommendations. Strong critical thinking, communication, and stakeholder partnership skills. Ability to manage complex analytical work independently with sound judgment and accountability. Qualifications - Preferred Bachelor’s degree in analytics, information systems, computer science, mathematics, statistics, business analytics, or a related field. Healthcare or payer analytics experience involving claims, membership, clinical operations, utilization management, provider data, or regulatory reporting. Experience supporting executive reporting and operational performance management. Experience improving data quality, reporting infrastructure, or analytical processes. jobs.title: Risk Analyst - Market Risk and Earnings Analysis
jobs.jd: At the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago, employees come first - that’s why we offer a highly competitive compensation and bonus package, and access to a comprehensive benefits program designed to meet the needs of our employees. C ollaborative, in-office operating model Retirement program (401k and Pension) Medical, dental and vision insurance Lifestyle Spending Account Competitive PTO plan 11 paid holidays per year ​ Who we are: Our mission at FHLBank Chicago: To partner with our members in Illinois and Wisconsin to provide them competitively priced funding, a reasonable return on their investment, and support for their community investment activities. Simply said, we're a bank for banks and other financial institutions, focused on being a strategic partner for our members and working together to reinvest in our communities, from urban centers to rural areas. Created by Congress in 1932, FHLBank Chicago is one of 11 Federal Home Loan Banks, government sponsored in support of mortgage lending and community investment. What it’s like to work here: At FHLBank Chicago, we bring people together. Our regular All-Staff meetings keep employees informed and our values drive the work that we do. Our Buddy Program pairs new hires with tenured employees to guide their onboarding. Through our Office of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI), we host signature and employee-led events to celebrate our differences and learn from each other and identify volunteer opportunities to strengthen our communities; and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) and culture teams create connections around shared interests and experiences. We offer live and on-demand professional development opportunities to grow your skillset and your career. What you’ll do: As a Quantitative Analyst in Market Risk and Earnings Analysis, you will work with stakeholders across the organization, including Capital Markets, Business Development, Finance, and Balance Sheet Management, to measure, monitor, and analyze the financial risks faced by the Bank. You will perform quantitative risk and earnings analysis, support risk limit monitoring and reporting, contribute to income simulation and strategic planning, and help develop advanced risk dashboards and analytics for senior management. How you’ll make an impact: Improve risk monitoring by designing efficient and scalable processes that provide timely visibility into risk exposures and trends. Deliver proactive quantitative analysis to identify emerging risks and support evolving modeling needs driven by market conditions, regulatory developments, and management priorities. Support strategic decision-making by partnering with Capital Markets, and other stakeholders on income forecasting and planning. Modernize risk analytics by applying advanced visualization, data, and analytical tools to improve reporting, automation, and management insights. What you can expect: Perform quantitative analysis of the Bank’s market risk exposures, earnings sensitivity, and key risk drivers . Monitor risk limits, exposures, sensitivities, and emerging trends and communicate results to management. Partner with internal stakeholders on model enhancements, methodology changes, and system/version upgrades , including testing and impact analysis. Support the reengineering and automation of risk and performance dashboards leveraging advanced visualization tools and AI across large datasets. Prepare analysis, reporting, and presentations for internal committees, management discussions, and risk meetings . Support the CFO organization during the annual Strategic Planning process, including additional risk and stress scenarios within the income forecasting and risk analysis framework . Collaborate with Capital Markets and other departments on new products, investment opportunities, and hedging strategies, including analysis of potential earnings and risk impacts. Support process reengineering, model documentation, controls, and End-User Computing (EUC) maintenance. Perform other duties as assigned. What you’ll bring: 1–3 years of experience in risk management, quantitative risk modeling, asset/liability management, fixed-income analytics, or capital markets. Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative or related field such as Mathematical Finance, Computational Finance, Computer Science, Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, or Accounting. Master’s degree preferred. CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst) or FRM (Financial Risk Manager) designation, or progress toward either designation, is a plus. Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into clear business insights. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented, collaborative, and comfortable managing multiple priorities and deliverables. Experience with Python and/or SQL preferred. Experience with Tableau, Databricks, or similar data and visualization platforms preferred. Knowledge of fixed-income products, interest-rate risk, income simulation, scenario analysis, or balance-sheet risk management is a plus. Salary Range: $75,325.00 - $125,500.00 The above represents the expected salary range for this job requisition. Ultimately, in determining your pay, we may also consider your experience, and other job-related factors. In addition to the base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package which can be found here: https://hrportal.ehr.com/fhlbc

jobs.title: SEM Analyst
jobs.jd: Our SEM Analysts are responsible for driving customer acquisition and lead generation through the planning, execution, and optimization of paid search and digital advertising campaigns. This position can be filled as an Associate SEM Analyst or an SEM Analyst based on the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate. What You'll Do As an SEM Analyst, you will manage search marketing initiatives across platforms such as Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising, as well as additional channels including Display, YouTube, Retargeting, and Performance Max. In addition, you will: Plan, launch, and optimize paid search campaigns across major platforms, including Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising. Support additional digital channels such as Display, YouTube, Retargeting, and Performance Max to drive acquisition goals. Perform keyword research to identify high‑value opportunities and ensure strong query coverage. Improve campaign performance through landing page evaluation and recommendations for UX, content, and conversion-rate enhancements. Develop and test ad copy, creative variations, and audience strategies to improve engagement and ROI. Monitor campaign pacing, performance trends, and budget allocation to ensure efficiency and goal alignment. Analyze fluctuations in traffic, conversion rates, and lead quality to identify root causes and propose corrective actions. Build and maintain tracking infrastructure, including tagging, conversion events, and platform integrations. Create cross‑channel performance dashboards and standardized reporting for internal stakeholders. Translate data insights into clear recommendations that support marketing, sales, and broader business objectives. Collaborate with analytics, creative, and channel teams to support integrated marketing strategies and performance optimization. Stay current on platform updates, best practices, and competitive trends to inform future testing and campaign planning. What it Takes Bachelors Degree or equivalent work experience. jobs.jd: About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. Monitor fiat and digital asset liquidity, funding needs, and operational risk controls. Lead pilot execution from planning through launch, including governance, testing, vendor diligence, and operational readiness. Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, Engineering, and Operations teams to build scalable solutions. jobs.jd: Agency Dept of Health and Human Services Division Public Health Job Classification Title Program Coordinator IV (S) Position Number 65005913 Grade NC14 About Us The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is one of the largest, most complex agencies in the state, and has approximately 17,000 employees. It is responsible for ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of all North Carolinians, providing human service needs for special populations including individuals who are deaf, blind, developmentally disabled, and mentally ill, and helping poor North Carolinians achieve economic independence. Description of Work The HIV/AIDS Data Quality Consultant supports statewide HIV surveillance by maintaining accurate, timely data within the electronic HIV/AIDS Reporting System (eHARS) and the NC Electronic Disease Surveillance System (NC EDSS). The position evaluates reporting workflows, identifies cases requiring regional follow‑up, and ensures rapid turnaround of information to support timely field investigation. This role also serves as the primary contact for Pediatric HIV surveillance activities and assists with data collection and documentation for pediatric cases. The Consultant provides technical expertise on required data submissions, system integration needs, and program reporting requirements. The position operates in a fast‑paced environment that requires independent work planning, consistent communication, and strong data‑management skills. Key Duties Include: – Maintaining accurate, up‑to‑date HIV surveillance data in eHARS and NC EDSS to support statewide reporting requirements. – Evaluating case‑report workflows to determine which reports require regional follow‑up and ensuring timely referral for field investigation. – Serving as the primary contact for Pediatric HIV surveillance activities and coordinating data collection for pediatric cases. – Reviewing incoming case information and ensuring rapid turnaround so field staff can locate and interview individuals as quickly as possible. – Compiling, printing, and preparing data sets for program management and surveillance reporting needs. – Communicating clearly and concisely with program partners regarding data needs, reporting timelines, and documentation requirements. – Supporting the preparation and submission of required monthly data transmissions to CDC and verifying technical accuracy. – Identifying opportunities to improve business processes, reporting workflows, and data‑system integration. – Coordinating with internal program staff to resolve data discrepancies, address reporting issues, and maintain data quality standards. – Managing self‑directed daily work while ensuring adherence to required timelines, quality standards, and confidentiality expectations. The Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)/ Management Preferences are not required. Applicants who possess the following skills are preferred: • Experience interpreting and applying public health reporting regulations for STD/HIV/AIDS cases in North Carolina, including policies related to disease control and case‑management protocols. • Demonstrated experience using eHARS and NC EDSS to enter, review, and update HIV and STD surveillance data, including the application of morbidity statistics and public health program evaluation principles. • Experience preparing and delivering clear written and verbal communications to diverse audiences and contributing to program planning or needs‑assessment activities that support unit objectives. • Demonstrated success reviewing and processing detailed surveillance reports and evaluating data‑processing workflows to identify errors, ensure accuracy, and support system improvement. • Experience working collaboratively with team members to resolve surveillance‑processing issues, coordinate information flow, and maintain consistent data‑quality standards. • Demonstrated commitment to maintaining strict confidentiality and secure handling of sensitive patient information in accordance with public health privacy requirements.
