jobs.jd: TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, empowers organizations with full AI visibility and consolidated security that inspires confidence, drives innovation, and eliminates risk. At TrendAI™, we’re always seeking exceptional talent; people who want to collaborate with the best and push boundaries together. Here, your work goes beyond building a career. You will help protect what matters and play a vital role in shaping a safer, more trustworthy AI-powered future. AI Fearlessly. Location: This is a hybrid role based out of our Las Colinas office and requires in-office presence 3 days per week. Position Summary: TrendAI is seeking an early-career Business Intelligence Engineer to join the team and turn product, operational, and security data into reliable, decision-ready insight. This role you be provided with close mentorship from experienced data and analytics engineers as you build your foundation in BI engineering. You will help build the data models, pipelines, and dashboards that business stakeholders rely on. You will learn how our data is structured, how it flows from source systems to reporting, and how small data issues can change a business decision. What You'll Do: Write and maintain SQL queries, data models, and transformations that power dashboards and recurring reports. Build and maintain repeatable, scripted pipelines for extracting and transforming data, avoiding one-off manual steps that can't be rerun or audited. Build and maintain dashboards and reports for business stakeholders. Translate business questions into clear technical requirements, working with analysts, engineers, and product partners. Reconcile data across sources and document discrepancies rather than silently choosing one. Validate data accuracy, investigate discrepancies, and monitor data quality over time. Treat missing or failed data as unknown and flag it, so a gap is never reported as a confirmed zero or "none found." Record provenance, metric definitions, and confidence levels so stakeholders can tell verified figures from inferred ones. Test pipelines under realistic conditions (volume, rate limits, source failures) before committing to a design. Support ad hoc analysis requests and help prioritize them alongside planned work. Contribute to team standards for code review, version control, and documentation. Grow your skills on with a path toward owning datasets end to end. Proactively communicate to business stakeholders or request owner to make sure the outcomes deliver on time and on quality. What You Should Have: Experience in computer science, data science, statistics, information systems, business analytics, or a related field. Working proficiency in SQL, including joins, aggregations, and window functions. Understanding of core data modeling concepts such as dimensional modeling and star schemas, gained through coursework, projects, or internships. Familiarity with at least one data visualization tool. Ability to verify outputs against independent sources and to explain how you checked your work. Comfort working with source systems that are poorly documented or change without notice, such as inspecting web application behavior or undocumented APIs. Experience using AI tools in analysis work while independently validating their output. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain data findings to non-technical audiences. What Will Make You Stand Out: Internship or project experience building dashboards, reports, or data pipelines. Python scripting for data extraction, validation, or automation. Exposure to data quality checks, testing, or audit-trail practices. Exposure to cloud data warehouses (such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift) or transformation tools (such as dbt or Airflow). Interest in cybersecurity, cloud, or AI products and the data they generate. What We Offer You: You're important to us. What matters to you, matters to us too. jobs.title: Scientist, Machine Learning (Human Physiology)
jobs.jd: ABOUT FLAGSHIP PIONEERING Flagship Pioneering is a platform innovation company that conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life sciences and technology companies. Since its founding in 2000, Flagship has originated over 100 scientific ventures and has deployed over $3 billion in capital toward the development of transformative life science businesses. Flagship's current portfolio of more than 35 companies includes Moderna, Generate Biomedicines, Sail Biomedicines, iris labs, and Extuitive. ABOUT FL127 FL127 is a privately held, early-stage company operating within the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem. The company is developing a first-in-category platform anchored in novel device technology. FL127 is building its scientific and technical foundation through a hypothesis-driven experimental program. We are assembling a lean team of scientists and engineers who work at the intersection of hardware, software, and physiology, and who want to build in an era when AI agents are first-class members of the team. THE ROLE FL127 is seeking a scientist to help connect the physiological signals our platform measures to what they indicate about a person. You will ground each signal in physiology, help design the human studies that test what it reflects, and build models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes in small human cohorts. Our imaging and signal-extraction team produces the measurements. Your work starts from those outputs. You will co-design human studies with that team so a single study informs both measurement quality and interpretation. FL127 is an AI-native company. Team members direct AI agents in their daily work for literature synthesis, study design, data analysis, and code. We are looking for someone who wants to work this way. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Ground each measured signal in physiology: what it reflects, what confounds it, and which physiological states it may indicate Work with the product and market team to decide which applications to study first, weighing scientific plausibility, study cost, and user value Co-design human studies with the imaging team, including endpoints, reference measurements, and protocols Build and evaluate models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes on small cohorts, with attention to confounders, leakage, demographic stratification, and sample size Set the evidence bar a finding must meet before it shapes the product, and report what the data supports and where it falls short Review extracted signals for physiological plausibility and suggest improvements to the measurement pipeline REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS PhD in biomedical engineering, physiology, bioengineering, biophotonics, or a related field, or an MD/PhD, with substantial applied machine learning experience Deep knowledge of human physiology in an area such as microcirculation, hemodynamics, tissue optics, skin biology, or cardiorespiratory physiology Experience taking a measurement or digital biomarker through human studies, including endpoint selection, reference measurements, IRB-governed protocols, and agreement analysis Statistical modeling on small human datasets, including within-subject and longitudinal designs Proficiency in Python and the modern ML stack, and comfort working inside an existing research codebase Enough imaging and signal-processing background to reason about how calibration, registration, and sampling affect a derived measurement Ability to work independently in an early-stage, ambiguous environment and make decisions with incomplete data PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Published or applied work in remote physiological sensing, digital biomarkers, or wearable or contactless measurement Experience turning research results into a product feature, ideally at a consumer device company Familiarity with skin optics models (Monte Carlo simulation, diffusion theory, chromophore decomposition) Experience modeling individual baselines and change over time Experience in a venture-backed startup or early-stage research environment WHY FL127 Work with human study data from your first weeks Shape which applications the company studies and builds first Join a small team where scientists and AI agents work side by side Draw on the scientific, operational, and capital resources of the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem jobs.title: Data Scientist, Cloud Distribution & Growth
jobs.jd:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

 - Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

jobs.title: Quantitative Researcher
jobs.jd: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description Your Team Macro & Quantitative Research is a central research group within Invesco Fixed Income. The team covers macro strategy, including U.S. rates and foreign exchange, quantitative portfolio management, systematic research, and quantitative infrastructure. We develop models, analytics, and research tools used by portfolio managers across fundamental credit, rates, securitized, multi-sector, and systematic investment teams. The team works collaboratively to translate investment research into practical portfolio applications. Your Role As a Senior Quantitative Researcher, you will serve as a quantitative research partner to portfolio managers across Invesco Fixed Income. You will conduct empirical research on fixed income markets, macroeconomic drivers, and relative-value opportunities and translate your findings into portfolio construction, asset allocation, and risk-management applications. You will independently lead research projects from hypothesis development and testing through implementation and production deployment. You will work closely with portfolio managers, economists, traders, fundamental analysts, and quantitative engineers across the fixed income platform. You Will Be Responsible For: Conducting empirical research on fixed income markets, macroeconomic drivers, relative value, and cross-asset relationships and translating the findings into actionable investment frameworks. Building tactical and strategic sector and asset-allocation models across credit, rates, securitized products, and emerging markets that connect macroeconomic and market views to portfolio positioning. Designing and improving portfolio-construction and optimization frameworks for fundamental and systematic portfolios, incorporating transaction costs, liquidity, turnover, concentration, and other practical investment constraints. Developing risk, scenario-analysis, and performance-attribution tools that improve investment decision-making and provide transparency into return drivers, factor exposures, and tracking error. Partnering with portfolio managers, traders, economists, and other investment professionals to translate investment ideas into scalable research, analytics, and portfolio-implementation frameworks. Developing shared research tools, reusable analytical libraries, and data pipelines using production-quality code, version control, testing, documentation, and peer review. Supporting the research, design, and launch of new fixed income strategies and contributing to client-facing research, presentations, and investment materials. Leading defined research projects, mentoring junior colleagues, and contributing to consistent standards for research design, testing, documentation, and production implementation. The Experience You Bring: Seven or more years of quantitative research experience in fixed income or multi-asset investing at an asset manager, hedge fund, bank, insurance company, pension fund, or index provider. A master’s degree or PhD in statistics, financial engineering, economics, operations research, mathematics, physics, computer science, or another relevant quantitative discipline. Advanced Python skills, including experience with analytical libraries such as pandas or Polars, NumPy, SciPy, and statsmodels, together with strong SQL skills and working knowledge of Git. Practical experience with factor models, time-series econometrics, portfolio optimization, and empirical investment research. Strong knowledge of fixed income instruments and risk, including duration, yield curves, credit spreads, credit quality, liquidity, and benchmark-relative risk. Experience taking quantitative research from hypothesis development and testing through implementation in a live investment or production environment. Ability to independently solve complex research problems, exercise sound judgment, evaluate alternative approaches, and clearly communicate recommendations. Ability to explain complex quantitative concepts to non-quantitative investment professionals, build consensus, and work effectively across fundamental, quantitative, and technical teams. Preferred Experience Experience supporting fundamental fixed income portfolio managers or conducting multi-sector allocation research, including macro-conditioned models, risk budgeting, or long-horizon return forecasting. Systematic credit or rates experience involving bond-level factor signals, TRACE data, index-constituent data, liquidity analysis, or transaction-cost modeling. Experience with institutional risk and portfolio platforms such as Aladdin, Bloomberg PORT, BarraOne, or Axioma and fixed income data from providers such as Bloomberg or ICE. Experience applying machine-learning techniques with disciplined validation and economic interpretation in noisy financial datasets. Familiarity with cloud data platforms, scalable quantitative research environments, and AI-assisted development and research tools. CFA designation or progress toward the designation. Full Time / Part Time Full time Worker Type Employee Job Exempt (Yes / No) Yes Workplace Model Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. jobs.title: Financial Systems Analyst
jobs.jd: We’re looking for someone who enjoys digging into data, untangling complex processes and building solutions that make work simpler and smarter. Experience in accounting, financial analysis, data analytics, process improvement or technology-enabled operations can all translate well to this role. What matters most is your ability to dig into data, understand complex processes and turn what you learn into practical solutions. Specifically, we’re looking for: Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas, scalable models and automation. Strong quantitative, analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience working with data to spot trends, investigate exceptions and support business decisions. An ability to break down complex processes and turn them into practical solutions. A knack for learning new technology and finding smarter ways to work. Experience with SQL, Python, Tableau, AI-enabled tools or similar technologies is a plus. About the Role: As a Financial Systems Analyst, you’ll partner closely with our Accounting team to make the way we work simpler, smarter and more scalable. You’ll get to know our existing processes, dig into the data behind them and look for opportunities to reduce repetitive work, strengthen controls and improve reporting. Then, you’ll help turn those opportunities into solutions using tools like SQL, Excel, Tableau, Python and AI-enabled technologies. The goal? Help our Accounting team spend less time preparing recurring reports and more time understanding the story behind the numbers. Here’s a snapshot of what you’d be doing: Partner with the Accounting team to understand existing workflows and identify manual work, reporting gaps, data risks and opportunities for improvement. Recommend and prioritize solutions based on business impact, risk and efficiency. Design, build, test and maintain reports, dashboards, data queries, Excel automations and other scalable tools. Validate your work to make sure solutions are accurate, reliable and built to last. Explore thoughtful ways to use AI, automation and emerging technologies to improve accounting workflows. Help establish appropriate controls around new tools and support teammates as they adopt new solutions. Jump into financial and data analysis, special projects and cross-functional work as business needs evolve. Pitch in wherever needed, excluding licensed activity, to help make the team and culture stronger. About You: Curiosity comes naturally to you. When you see a process that takes five steps, you can’t help but wonder if it could take three. You enjoy solving problems and aren’t afraid to dig into the details to figure out what’s really going on. You can work with both technical and non-technical teammates and explain complicated ideas in a way that makes sense. You’re comfortable working independently, but you know the best solutions often come from working together. You can handle confidential financial information with care and good judgment. And when priorities change? You can adapt, refocus and keep things moving. Please note: This position does not offer employment-based immigration sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and able to maintain work authorization without company sponsorship. About Us: We’re all about helping Veterans and military families become homeowners. In two short decades, we closed over 500,000 VA Loans and became the #1 VA lender for homebuyers in the nation. But to us, success isn’t measured in numbers. Our success is measured in living our values every day: Be Passionate and Have Fun, Deliver Results with Integrity and Enhance Lives Every Day. We always strive to provide friendly service to military homebuyers and their families. And we always seek to lift up people and communities across the country. We’re so glad you’re here checking out this opportunity! If this role gets you excited but you’re worried you don’t check every box – don't sweat it. We’re more interested in what you can bring to the team than a perfect checklist. If you’re passionate, driven, and ready to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Come as you are, and together we’ll create something amazing. Interested? Apply Today! Learn more about Veterans United on Glassdoor and our career site at vu.com/careers Veterans United Home Loans and its affiliates are Equal Opportunity Employers that consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, transgender status, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability or genetic information.

jobs.title: Revenue Cycle Continuous Improvement Analyst
jobs.jd: Huron helps its clients drive growth, enhance performance and sustain leadership in the markets they serve. We help healthcare organizations build innovation capabilities and accelerate key growth initiatives, enabling organizations to own the future, instead of being disrupted by it. Together, we empower clients to create sustainable growth, optimize internal processes and deliver better consumer outcomes. Health systems, hospitals and medical clinics are under immense pressure to improve clinical outcomes and reduce the cost of providing patient care. Investing in new partnerships, clinical services and technology is not enough to create meaningful and substantive change. To succeed long-term, healthcare organizations must empower leaders, clinicians, employees, affiliates and communities to build cultures that foster innovation to achieve the best outcomes for patients. Joining the Huron team means you’ll help our clients evolve and adapt to the rapidly changing healthcare environment and optimize existing business operations, improve clinical outcomes, create a more consumer-centric healthcare experience, and drive physician, patient and employee engagement across the enterprise. Join our team as the expert you are now and create your future. Huron Managed Services is currently seeking an AR Insights Analyst to join Adventist Health’s Continuous Improvement and Insights (CI&I) team. The AR Insights Analyst will provide strategic data insights and reporting to financial clearance, registration, and hospital revenue cycle operations leaders across the system. They will complete detailed AR and metric research, identify root cause issues impacting bottom-line performance, and collaborate with colleagues and leaders across Adventist to develop strategies that enhance performance and drive operational improvement. HURON PROFILE Huron is a consultancy that helps our clients drive growth, enhance performance, and achieve sustainable results. We partner with healthcare organizations to develop strategies, implement solutions, and improve operational performance. As a Continuous Improvement & Insights Analyst within Huron Managed Service s , you will support ongoing efforts to improve revenue cycle performance through data analysis, operational insights, and continuous improvement. Working closely with Huron team members and operational leaders, you will analyze performance trends, monitor key performance indicators, identify opportunities for improvement, and help translate data into actionable solutions. This role is ideal for someone who combines strong analytical skills with an understanding of healthcare revenue cycle operations and enjoys turning complex data into meaningful insights. You will help teams identify performance gaps, understand root causes, implement improvement initiatives, and measure results to support sustainable operational performance. KEY JOB DUTIES Analyze, interprets, and summarizes pertinent revenue cycle data components, and monitors performance against Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to identify process improvement opportunities Conducts risk assessments to achieving KPI targets, reports identified risks to management, and provides recommendations for mitigation of risk Extrapolates market and payer trends and coordinates with operational leaders, managed care, vendor management, and other relevant stakeholders to support development of action plans to attain top decile metric performance Supports execution of metric improvement solutions by providing operational leaders with necessary data and insights to take targeted actions Facilitates cross-market collaboration and issue resolution, leveraging system-wide exposure to derive and support delivery of optimal solutions Prepares status reports and action-oriented summaries for executive leaders across the system Attends metric and project calls with Senior Management and support staff Utilizes enhanced analytical tools for high volume, complex analyses, to provide critical insights and process updates based on analysis and collaboration with operational leaders QUALIFICATIONS Core Qualifications Current permanent U.S. work authorization required Bachelor's degree required Limited travel required Advanced or highly proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) 3-5 years of relevant healthcare and/or consulting experience Preferred Experience Relevant hospital or physician revenue cycle experience with a focus on data analysis and performance improvement initiatives, OR Project leadership and workplan management experience within a consulting firm setting with a focus on hospital or physician revenue cycle, denials management, or patient access services Candidate Qualities Possesses strong operational understanding of revenue cycle processes and metrics Proven critical thinking skills in both data collection and complex analysis; ability to identify data gaps and risks, develop sound conclusions, and create implementable and sustainable recommendations for improvement Demonstrated ability to effectively prioritize and manage multiple concurrent tasks with a high sense urgency across one or more workstreams Professional and polished written and verbal communication skills; ability to effectively summarize information and present findings and recommendations to internal and client leadership; skilled at interactions with varying levels of client personal from staff to leadership Ability to design and apply conceptual models to business problems to understand issues and support with reporting and analytics Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment The estimated salary range for this job is $70,000 - $94,000. The actual salary paid to an individual will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to specific skills or certifications, years of experience, market changes and required travel. jobs.jd: ANDERSEN CORPORATION SUMMARY: At Andersen, we see possibility everywhere, every day and in everything we do. This role develops and maintains standard people reporting, self-service dashboards, and reporting tools while ensuring data integrity, consistency, and governance standards. The analyst serves as a trusted partner to HR, business leaders, and HRIS teams by translating workforce data into meaningful reporting solutions that support organizational effectiveness. Deliver standardized people metrics and reporting packages for managers, HR leaders, and business stakeholders. Generate reports related to headcount, turnover, hiring, retention, demographics, talent movement, and other workforce metrics. Ensure reports are delivered accurately and within established service-level expectations. Dashboard & Self-Service Reporting Development 20% Design, develop, and maintain self-service reporting tools and dashboards. Create user-friendly reporting solutions that enable leaders to independently access workforce information. Partner with HR and business stakeholders to identify reporting requirements and prioritize enhancements. Continuously improve reporting accessibility, usability, and data visualization effectiveness. Reporting Governance & Documentation 20% Maintain reporting documentation, business rules, data definitions, and reporting procedures. Support governance processes to ensure consistent use of people metrics across the organization. Establish and maintain reporting standards and best practices. Document report logic, calculations, and data sources to support transparency and scalability. Data Quality & Integrity 15% Monitor reporting accuracy, consistency, and data reliability across workforce reports. Validate workforce metrics and investigate reporting discrepancies. Partner with HRIS, People Analytics, and Data Governance teams to resolve data issues. Support audit and validation processes to improve confidence in workforce reporting. Stakeholder Partnership 10% Collaborate with HR Business Partners, Centers of Excellence, HR Operations, and business leaders to understand reporting needs. Employee Resource Groups, which provide access to leaders, relevant volunteer and mentoring opportunities, and interactions with counterparts in industry groups and client organizations. jobs.title: Claims Analyst
jobs.jd: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re hiring a Claims Analyst to own the day-to-day integrity of our claims and adjudication workflows and to help build the processes, controls, and reporting behind them. This is a hands-on role: you’ll personally work our hardest claims and denials while standing up the playbooks, benchmarks, and dashboards that let claims operations scale without breaking. Reporting to our Manager, RCM, you’ll sit at the intersection of our clearinghouse, prior-auth, and finance systems — and you’ll be the person who can explain exactly why a claim paid, denied, or landed where it did. What you'll do: Own claims adjudication and QA. Review, validate, and adjudicate imaging claims against benefit designs, contracted rates, and our pass-through payment model; identify and resolve pricing, coding, and eligibility discrepancies before they become client or member issues. Lead denials management. Investigate root causes of denials and underpayments, drive appeals and resubmissions, and build recurring analysis that turns denial patterns into fixes upstream (prior auth, eligibility, EDI configuration). Manage EDI and clearinghouse workflows. Work hands-on in Waystar across 837P submissions, 835 remittances, and companion-guide requirements; troubleshoot rejections and payer-specific edits; partner with vendors to keep the pipes clean. Safeguard cost-share and accumulator accuracy. Ensure deductible, coinsurance, HDHP, and accumulator logic is applied correctly so members and clients are billed accurately and we stay compliant with cost-sharing rules. Own AR and aging. Monitor accounts receivable and claims aging, prioritize collectible balances, and maintain reporting that gives finance and leadership a real-time view of what’s outstanding and why. Build the reporting layer. Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs (adjudication turnaround, denial rate, clean-claim rate, AR aging, recovery rate) from Waystar and adjacent claims data. Coordinate across the stack. Work closely with prior authorization (Infinx), finance, and client-facing teams to close the loop between authorization, exam, claim, and payment. Write the playbook. Document repeatable SOPs, edits, and escalation paths, and help train and mentor analysts as the team grows. About you: Required 2+ years in healthcare claims, revenue cycle, or medical billing, with demonstrated ownership of complex adjudication and denials work Deep hands-on experience with EDI transactions (837/835) and a clearinghouse platform (Waystar strongly preferred) Strong command of CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, place-of-service, and modifier logic — ideally in radiology/imaging Working knowledge of benefit structures, cost-sharing, deductibles, and accumulator/HDHP mechanics Advanced spreadsheet skills and comfort building reporting from raw claims data A meticulous, audit-minded approach: you can trace any dollar to its source and defend it Preferred Experience at a TPA, benefits administrator, or payer, especially serving self-funded employers Familiarity with prior authorization workflows and tools (e.g., Infinx) Exposure to appeals, payer escalations, and underpayment recovery at scale Early-stage or high-growth environment experience — comfortable building process where none exists The salary range for this position is $50,000 - $65,000. This position is also bonus eligible. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. jobs.jd: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Analyst, Risk Adjustment to join our Risk Adjustment team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: Risk Adjustment accounts for differences in members’ health needs and expected cost of care. Accurate and complete clinical documentation helps ensure that a member’s health status is appropriately represented. Prospective Risk Adjustment focuses on proactively supporting opportunities for healthcare providers to review members’ health information and accurately document conditions addressed during clinical care, in accordance with applicable clinical coding and documentation requirements. These efforts may include sharing relevant clinical information with providers at the point of care, conducting virtual or in-home health assessments, and providing reports that identify historical or suspected conditions for provider review and clinical validation. The Analyst, Risk Adjustment supports the day-to-day execution and performance of Prospective Risk Adjustment programs. This role partners with internal teams and external vendors to ensure operational workflows are functioning as intended, program data and reporting are accurate, claims are processed appropriately, and operational issues are identified and resolved in a timely manner. The analyst will support a portfolio of initiatives including Point-of-Care tools, Virtual Health Assessments (VHA), In-Home Assessments (IHA), and provider reporting to support the review of member conditions. This role is well suited for an analytical, detail-oriented professional interested in developing expertise in Risk Adjustment and healthcare operations. You will report into the Sr. Manager, Strategic Initiatives (Risk Adjustment). Work Location: This position is based in our New York, NY office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $75,348- $98,894 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Prospective Risk Adjustment Program Operations (30%) – Support daily operations across prospective Risk Adjustment programs, including Point-of-Care tooling, VHA, IHA, and provider gap-reporting initiatives. Monitor program activity and workflows to ensure processes are functioning as intended; investigate operational issues and coordinate resolution or escalation as appropriate. Vendor Operations & Support (25%) – Support the day-to-day operational needs of external vendors. Coordinate recurring deliverables and data exchanges, respond to operational questions, track issues and action items, and partner with vendors and internal stakeholders to drive timely resolution. Perform data validation and reconciliation across internal and vendor data sources to identify discrepancies, trends, and opportunities for operational improvement. Point-of-Care & Provider Programs (15%) – Support programs that provide relevant member health information, including historical and suspected conditions, to healthcare providers for review and clinical validation. Support Point-of-Care tools and provider reporting initiatives and assist with resolving related data, reporting, and workflow issues. Member & Claims Operations (10%) – Support member-level program operations, including reviewing and processing appropriate exclusions from VHA and IHA programs. Monitor and reconcile claims associated with prospective Risk Adjustment initiatives to ensure appropriate processing and payment; investigate discrepancies and partner with relevant teams to support resolution. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and recurring deliverables. jobs.title: Intelligence Systems Analyst
jobs.jd:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We also draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

I2 Engineering works hand in hand with I2’s analysts and investigators, building tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish. Our tools help them make sense of vast and complex datasets, discover and measure on-platform and off-platform risk, and investigate severe misuse with greater speed, depth, and consistency.


About the Role

We are looking for an Intelligence Systems Analyst who wants to work alongside investigators to understand difficult cases, contribute to analysis, and build tools and workflows that help the team do more. As investigators pursue leads, assess risks, and determine what happened, you’ll see where better tools could help and build them.

The role combines hands-on software and data work with meaningful participation in investigations. Depending on the problem, you might trace activity across internal systems, write a query or small application, prototype an AI-assisted workflow, improve how evidence is assembled, or turn an investigator’s recurring need into a durable product capability.

You will work closely with engineers, analysts, investigators, and other subject matter experts. Success requires enough operational understanding to contribute meaningfully to an investigation and enough technical ownership to build solutions that remain useful after the immediate case is resolved.


In this role, you will:

 - Work directly alongside investigators on complex cases, helping develop leads, analyze evidence, and identify useful technical approaches.

 - Build and maintain software, data workflows, and internal tools that accelerate investigations of potential high-severity misuse or harm.

 - Use Python, SQL, and internal data systems to gather, connect, and analyze information relevant to investigative work.

 - Apply OpenAI’s models to research, search, triage, synthesis, and evidence review in workflows that keep expert investigators informed and in control.

 - Turn recurring investigative bottlenecks into reliable tools, automation, and product capabilities that support multiple users and cases.

 - Prototype quickly when a new investigative question arises, then improve reliability, usability, and maintainability as requirements become clearer.

 - Respect the privacy, permissions, evidence-handling requirements, and operational safeguards that accompany sensitive investigative work.

 - Collaborate with teams across Applied, Safety Systems, Research, User Operations, and Strategy when their expertise or systems are needed.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience building and shipping software, internal tools, data workflows, or operational products.

 - Comfort working directly with investigators, analysts, or other subject matter experts in ambiguous or consequential situations.

 - Practical experience with Python, SQL, and structured or unstructured data.

 - The ability to investigate an unclear problem, follow evidence across systems, and turn what you learn into a practical next step.

 - Sound judgment about privacy, data access, evidence quality, and the consequences of getting an investigation wrong.

 - Interest in using AI systems to extend human investigative capability while keeping expert judgment central.

 - The flexibility to move between coding, analysis, investigative support, and close collaboration with technical and operational partners.

Experience in trust and safety, security, intelligence, investigations, or related domains is helpful but not required.

jobs.title: Vertical Sales Strategy and Operations
jobs.jd:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re looking for someone to join our Sales Strategy & Operations team and own how ElevenLabs goes to market by vertical. As we shift from a horizontal motion to a vertical-led one, you will go deep on each of our top verticals — the buyer, the use cases, the competitive landscape, and what it takes to win — and turn that into a repeatable playbook for launching and scaling each one.

As part of the Revenue Operations team, you'll sit at the center of the vertical GTM motion, working with Product Marketing, Forward Deployed Engineering, Product, and Sales leadership to define each vertical's strategy, surface product gaps, and drive cross-functional alignment until every vertical is launched and performing. This is a role for someone who wants to shape a new market from the ground up, not maintain an existing one.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

 - Vertical Deep Dives - Own the research and strategy for each top vertical: market sizing, ICP and persona definition, buying process, priority use cases, competitive positioning, and where ElevenLabs wins.

 - Vertical Launches - Run the end-to-end launch of each vertical, from strategy and segmentation through enablement, pipeline targets, and post-launch performance reviews.

 - Cross-Functional Alignment - Drive alignment across PMM, FDE, Product, Sales, and Marketing on vertical priorities, owners, and timelines. Be the single thread that keeps every function moving in the same direction.

 - Product Needs - Dig deep into what each vertical requires from the product — integrations, compliance, features, workflows, and translate field signal into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for Product.

 - Data-Driven Strategy - Define the metrics that matter for each vertical (pipeline, win rate, ACV, sales cycle, product adoption), build the dashboards, and use the insights to decide where to double down or pull back.

 - Leadership Partnership - Serve as a trusted advisor to Sales and GTM leadership on where to invest by vertical, with clear recommendations and regular performance reporting.
   
   

Who you are

We're looking for exceptional individuals who combine technical excellence with ethical awareness, who are excited by hard problems and motivated by human impact. You’ll strive with us if you:

 - Are passionate about audio AI driven by a desire to make content universally accessible and breaking the frontiers of new tech.

 - Are a highly motivated and driven individual with a strong work ethic. Our team is aware of this critical moment of audio AI evolution and is committed to going the extra mile to lead.

 - Are analytical, efficient, and strive on solving complex challenges with a first principles mindset.

 - Consistently strive for excellence, delivering high-quality work quickly and exceeding expectations.

 - Take initiative and work autonomously from day one, prioritizing learning and contribution while leaving ego aside.
   
   

What you bring

 - 4+ years in Sales Strategy & Operations or GTM strategy, ideally with experience building or launching a vertical GTM motion

 - Proven track record of taking an ambiguous strategic question to a structured answer, then driving execution across teams.

 - Deep curiosity about industries — you enjoy learning how a healthcare, financial services, or retail buyer actually operates and what they need

jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.jd:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.


THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM

The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication.

Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes.


THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions rather than implementing against a fixed specification. You'll validate ideas against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.


YOUR NORMAL EXPERIENCE

This is a hands-on research residency: you'll take ownership of a real technical problem in inference algorithms for in-memory compute, work alongside the researchers and engineers building our platform, and be expected to contribute ideas, not just execute someone else's. Your job is to help turn research into production-quality research code that a team can build on. Outside-of-the-box thinking is encouraged.

You'll get direct exposure to the pace, ambiguity, and speed of decision-making that comes with working at a fast-moving, well-funded startup, where the distance between an idea on a whiteboard and a result on real hardware is measured in weeks, not years.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop inference algorithms for in-memory hardware. Understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution and develop algorithms that exploit it natively, demonstrated first in simulation and then on hardware.

Design numerical methods that fit the physics. Design methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.

Build evaluation suites and benchmarks. Help build the evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize how algorithms behave on real hardware and in simulation, and tell us honestly whether any of it actually works.

Translate workloads into hardware constraints. Turn insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for the hardware and architecture teams.

Prototype and iterate rapidly. Move with the hardware as it evolves from simulation to FPGA to silicon.

Drive a research question of your own. Partner with researchers and engineers to scope, run, and iterate on an original technical investigation, with rigorous experimental analysis and documentation along the way.

Co-author a paper. Work with the team to write up your findings for submission to a relevant venue, with mentorship on framing, experiments, and technical writing. One of the two milestones every resident builds toward.

Present at the residency colloquium. Share your work and thinking with the broader Normal Computing research community at the program's capstone event, and get real-time feedback from people building this technology every day.


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A GREAT FIT

Currently pursuing or recently completed a graduate degree (MS or PhD, or equivalent research experience) in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field. Publications are a strong plus, but not required at the resident level; a solid research track record is what matters.

A working understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints. Deep production experience isn't expected at the resident level, but the intuition should feel familiar.

Some exposure to inference optimization (quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention), or to stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation.

Strong Python skills, plus some experience with a systems language (C++, Rust, or similar) or with implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks.

Some experience (course projects, research, or otherwise) turning a research idea into working, reasonably reproducible code. You care about whether results replicate, not just whether a demo works once.

Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently.

Bonus: exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures; publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing; or experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; prior experience writing up research (papers, theses, technical reports) is a plus, as is any experience presenting technical work to a live audience.

A bias toward ownership and self-direction. You're energized, not overwhelmed, by the ambiguity and speed of a small, fast-moving startup.

ABOUT SUPERHUMAN

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. THE OPPORTUNITY

Turn complex data into growth decisions that shape the future of Superhuman’s product suite.

As an Acquisition Data Scientist at Superhuman, you’ll shape how we acquire, activate, and expand our user base across a diverse portfolio of consumer and enterprise products. You’ll partner directly with Acquisition Marketing to improve the effectiveness of paid and organic channels, optimize the web funnel, and ensure every marketing dollar drives measurable growth.

You’ll tackle questions spanning budget allocation, channel attribution, SEO, AEO, cross-product activation, bundled offerings, and the full self-serve journey from first touch through activation and viral expansion.

You’ll be embedded in a cross-functional pod aligned to a Route to Market, working closely with Engineering, Finance, Marketing, Design, and User Research. With direct access to the leaders setting strategy, you’ll serve as the go-to data partner for acquisition: getting into the technical details, translating complex findings into clear recommendations on channel optimization, budget decisions, and new growth areas.

This role is for a hands-on data scientist who thrives in a fast-moving environment, enjoys solving complex growth problems, and wants their work to measurably influence outcomes across products, audiences, and go-to-market motions.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

This role is for someone who wants to be extremely hands-on, enjoys partnering cross-functionally with marketing peers, and wants to get deep into the technical weeds to find the best recommendations to ensure we optimize every marketing dollar we spend.

The university has pioneered a new way to learn in the 21st century, one that has received praise from academic, industry, government, and media leaders. Whatever your role, working for WGU gives you a part to play in helping students graduate, creating a better tomorrow for themselves and their families. They perform ad hoc analyses, build standard reports and data visualizations, and deliver information and insights through various methods and media that privilege data storytelling and compress time-to-action. As a Data Analyst, you will transform complex data into actionable insights that support program development, student engagement, and marketing effectiveness. Working cross-functionally with stakeholders across Program Development, Product, Decision Intelligence, Marketing, and Data Engineering, you will help drive meaningful outcomes through data-driven decision-making. What You'll Do Analyze large datasets to uncover trends and deliver actionable insights that inform program development, student engagement strategies, and marketing initiatives. Build, maintain, and enhance dashboards and data visualizations, including consolidating and improving existing reporting assets. Translate stakeholder needs and ambiguous business questions into technical requirements and data-driven solutions. Partner with Data Engineering to support ETL and data pipeline development while ensuring data quality and reliability. Perform ad hoc analyses and communicate findings through compelling data storytelling and recommendations. Apply descriptive statistics, translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical approaches, identify root causes and performance drivers, and develop actionable recommendations and analytical techniques to identify patterns, trends, and opportunities for improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Program Development, Product, Marketing, and Decision Intelligence to support strategic initiatives and drive business impact. Analyze customer journeys, marketing funnels, audience segments, and channel performance to identify drivers of acquisition, engagement, conversion, and downstream outcomes. Strong SQL skills and experience querying large datasets. Experience with Tableau or Power BI for data visualization. Experience working with ETL or ELT processes and data pipelines. Solid working knowledge of descriptive statistics and analytical methods, with the ability to apply them to real-world datasets Ability to apply sound judgment and analytical thinking to identify root causes of data issues and inform recommendations. Bonus Points Experience working with large-scale datasets containing millions of records. Familiarity with Databricks or similar data platforms. Proficiency in a programming language such as Python or R, experience with GitHub and analytics documentation standards, and experience contributing to dashboard optimization or consolidation projects. Experience with marketing, digital, or customer journey analytics, preferably with hands-on experience for Adobe Analytics and/or Adobe Customer Journey Analytics or other related platforms. Experience with marketing funnel measurement, attribution modeling, channel performance analysis, customer segmentation, and marketing experimentation and testing. Ability to translate ambiguous business problems into scalable technical and analytical solutions. Experience applying root cause analysis and diagnostic methodologies to identify drivers of business performance and data issues. Experience producing AI-assisted analytics, including leveraging AI-enabled tools and technologies to accelerate analysis, generate insights, enhance reporting, and support data-driven decision-making. Experience in Lieu of Education An equivalent combination of education and experience that demonstrates the required competencies may be considered. jobs.jd: Data Science Analyst Locations: Wilmington, DE; Charlotte, NC (Hybrid) As an Data Science Analyst, you’ll develop the technical skills to build the machine learning systems that drive our company and produce great customer outcomes. You’ll get hands-on experience as you apply your talents, creativity, and passion to create innovative solutions to real-world data science use cases. No matter the projects, you’ll have the opportunity to explore, while learning from experts in consumer lending in a close-knit team-oriented environment. This role will provide exposure across multiple disciplines to accelerate your career growth. In the Role: Apply diverse statistical and machine learning techniques to analyze a variety of datasets to solve complex, unstructured business problems. Actively contribute to our team’s vibrant culture through sharing knowledge, helping peers, and generally being a great person to work with. Develop creative technical solutions to improve the company’s decision making, the customer’s experience, and shareholder returns. Evaluate non-traditional data sources to see if they result in better underwriting decisions, saving our hard-working customers millions in interest payments. Mine the “digital exhaust” of our marketing campaigns to identify new populations who would benefit from our products. Partner with our operations teams to surface data insights that will allow our thousands of branch staff to better serve our customers. Requirements: Current post-graduate degree student in a quantitative discipline (Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Biostatistics, Physics, Economics, Operations Research, or Computer Science) with an expected graduation date of Winter 2026 or Spring 2027. Outstanding communication skills, including the ability to explain technical topics and concepts to a non-technical audience. Proven experience (in an academic, athletic, volunteer, or employment context) working with teams of diverse individuals to deliver complex projects. Experience in use of open-source machine learning libraries (Python or R). Innovative and capable of developing creative solutions to complex, data-driven problems. Preferred: Successful candidates will possess strong analytic, strategic thinking, communications, and leadership skills. They will also demonstrate curiosity, creative problem solving, integrative business thinking, teamwork, and bias for action. Just as importantly, they will be enthusiastic learners who want to tackle real-world challenges. About You: You are ready to launch your data science career. You want to create solutions to help hard-working Americans improve their financial lives. You want to work on a modern cloud-based data infrastructure. You want to directly learn from some of the best data science and business leaders in consumer finance. You want to be part of a team which is nimble, collaborative, diverse, and fun. Who we Are: OneMain Financial (NYSE: OMF) is the leader in offering nonprime customers responsible access to credit and is dedicated to improving the financial well-being of hardworking Americans. jobs.title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
jobs.jd:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.

 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.

 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.

 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.

 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.

 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.

 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.

 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - SQL or Python, which helps you work alongside engineers.

 - Specific, demonstrable use of AI to speed up analytical work, and real interest in teaching others to do the same.

 - Exposure to healthcare or regulated markets, or to European or multi-region expansion.

jobs.title: Pricing Strategy Analyst (Remote)
jobs.jd: We're looking for a Pricing Strategy Analyst to join Procore's Corporate Strategy team. In this role, you'll be the data and analytics engine behind our pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy, turning transaction, sales, and product data into the commercial signals that inform our decisions. You'll also lead smaller pricing initiatives across the full Procore portfolio, including our emerging AI offerings. The primary goal of this role is to make sure Procore's pricing decisions are grounded in clear, accurate, and well-sourced data. As a Pricing Strategy Analyst , you'll partner with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing to analyze how our pricing and packaging perform in the market and to build the visibility needed to improve them. Use your structured problem-solving, data analysis, and executive communication skills to shape how Procore captures value from what we build and buy. If you want hands-on work to drive top line growth and connect everyone in construction, apply today and join our team! This position reports to the Senior Manager of Pricing & Monetization Strategy and can be based remotely in the US. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead pricing and packaging initiatives from hypothesis through recommendation, in partnership with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing Build and stress-test the business case behind pricing decisions, including segment-level performance, cannibalization-adjusted ARR impact, and migration and monetization sizing. Analyze transaction, bookings, discounting, and product data to identify the commercial signals that explain how our pricing and packaging perform, and diagnose the root cause when they underperform, whether it is package design, sales execution, or market fit. Design and run market, competitive, and willingness-to-pay research, including win/loss and price elasticity analysis, to pressure-test pricing hypotheses before they reach leadership. Build and maintain pricing and packaging reporting and dashboards that give Product, Sales, and Finance visibility into performance, working with data teams to keep metrics and data sources accurate and consistent. Translate analysis into a small number of clear, claim-driven recommendations, present them to executive leaders, and defend them under challenge. Partner with Pricing Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, and Marketing to make sure approved decisions are operationalized and communicated to the field. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, strategy, business or data analytics, financial planning and analysis, or consulting wi th 2+ y ears inside a pricing or monetization practice at a top-tier strategy firm Track record of framing ambiguous problems into clear analytical frameworks and presenting recommendations to cross-functional and senior audiences. Experience leading projects or workstreams from analysis through recommendation, with the ability to balance multiple priorities. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, with experience building revenue impact and unit economics models. Hands-on experience querying and analyzing large datasets (e.g., SQL), building reports in a BI tool (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) is a plus Ability to synthesize qualitative inputs, such as call transcripts and field feedback, into clear themes that support pricing recommendations. Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills, with experience partnering with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing teams. Familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics (e.g., ARR, net revenue retention, win rate, discount rate) is a plus Curiosity, high agency, and an owner’s mindset with a strong bias for action. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 81,600.00 - 112,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. Cboe Predicts provides retail and institutional customers the ability to trade binary contracts that allow for risk transference based on realized events. The Analyst will conduct competitive analysis, build internal automation and tooling, and explore potential new prediction market offerings. The prediction market space is growing rapidly, with the analyst expected to provide strategic insights regarding major developments in the space. This role combines aspects of traditional capital market research with the opportunity for innovation in a rapidly growing space. This is a hands-on generalist seat with visible output. Expect to write analysis in the morning and code a Python script in the afternoon, and be comfortable integrating AI assisted workflows into daily routines. The analyst should be comfortable presenting and defending their ideas, comfortable with statistical analysis, financial theory, and objectively analyzing world events with their respective impacts at a macro and micro level. Experience in capital markets, derivatives, programming, writing research reports or academic papers is a plus. Your responsibilities will be: Customer Expansion Analysis Analyze retail participation, flow characteristics, and adoption trends across Cboe proprietary products — index options, mini and nano contracts, short-dated expiries — and translate patterns into product and go-to-market implications. Build and maintain recurring dashboards and reporting on retail behavior for internal business owners, replacing manual data pulls with automated pipelines. Quantify the impact of retail-facing initiatives — education, market protections, contract design changes, listing decisions — in dollar or participation terms suitable for advisory group and executive materials. Assist in tracking competitor product changes and fee filings; ensure internal stakeholders are informed on a timely basis. Monitor trends occurring across institutional clients, determining ways of measuring of their participation into event contracts to support Cboe Predicts Growth. Create reports around competitors and their activities related to institutional and retail customer strategy and product use-cases. Research alternative asset classes and adjacent product structures — digital assets, commodities, credit, event and prediction markets, private-market access vehicles, defined-outcome and derivative-income products — and assess where a listed, cleared, or exchange-adjacent offering is viable via event contracts or binary options wrappers. Monitor the regulatory and policy environment shaping retail access to alternatives; flag developments that open or close a path. Strong written communication skills Demonstrated ability to take a loosely scoped project to a concrete deliverable across multiple stakeholders. Reporting to the Fixed Income & Private Markets Data Value Stream Lead, this role is responsible for the management of our fixed income data sets, including reference data, corporate actions, ratings, and related datasets. The role combines domain expertise, data management, stakeholder collaboration, and operational excellence to ensure the organization generates trusted, scalable, and commercially valuable data products. Responsibilities Manage bond data products within the Fixed Income Data Group, including bond terms and conditions, corporate actions data, ensuring data quality, accuracy, and timely delivery for index production and maintenance. Work with the Fixed Income Index managers to deliver timely updates to securities within the relevant index universes. Conduct data quality checks, implement validation and verification processes, and maintain high standards of data quality. Collaborate with internal stakeholders and index managers to understand data requirements and ensure indices comply with their methodologies and objectives. Onboard new data feeds and data sets, ensuring seamless integration into existing systems and adherence to processes and quality metrics. Assist in preparing reports and presentations related to fixed income data analysis for internal and external clients. Provide timely and accurate responses to enquiries from clients. Proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis, manipulation, and visualization, with a willingness to further develop these skills in a financial data environment.
