Preferred Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, mathematics, data science, business, or a related field. jobs.location: Remote (US East Coast / Eastern Time Zone Preferred)
jobs.jd: Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team. Analytics Engineer We’re hiring Analytics Engineers to join Convene Hospitality Group’s (CHG) Technology organization. We’re building out the foundational platform to democratize data at CHG so that a venue GM, a finance lead, and an AI agent are all able to ask a question and get the same trusted answer. Analytics engineers own the full path from ingestion to visualization, including governance and observability. You’ll bring data in from source systems, model it through bronze, silver, and gold, define the semantic layer, and breathe life into the visualizations, conversational analytics, and business agents that teams rely on to make decisions. You’ll join the Data Platform team, reporting to its Engineering Manager, and work closely with other analytics engineers and business partners across the company. You’ll build on Snowflake, dbt, and Fivetran, using Snowflake-native capabilities like semantic views and Cortex to power ThoughtSpot and beyond. What You’ll Do: Partner with the business. Work with Finance, Sales, Operations, and venue teams to understand their needs and turn them into models and metrics they trust. Own ingestion for your domains. Set up and maintain Fivetran connectors, land data in bronze, and handle schema drift and load failures. Model the business. Build dbt models that move data through bronze, silver, and gold, and shape gold around how CHG runs so people outside the data team can understand and use it. Own the semantic layer. Set metrics, dimensions, and relationships so a number means the same thing in a dashboard, a search, or an agent’s answer. Tune synonyms and descriptions so a model picks the right measure, trace wrong answers to the root cause, and help us decide where each definition lives. Power self-service in ThoughtSpot. Build the models and Liveboards that let teams explore data on their own, and turn the questions people actually ask into new test cases. Own the quality of conversational analytics. Test answers the way you’d test code. Build and maintain a golden question set of real business questions paired with certified answers as your test cases, run them as a regression suite on every model or semantic change, and block releases that fail. Back your models with dbt tests and clear documentation. Apply governance day to day. Tag sensitive data at ingestion, apply access controls such as tag-based masking and row access policies, and follow the standards the team sets, so an agent only returns what the person asking is allowed to see. Keep it fast and fresh. Monitor freshness, data quality, and pipeline health so problems surface to you before they reach a dashboard or an agent’s answer. Tune query and model performance, from incremental dbt models to warehouse sizing, so answers come back fast and Snowflake costs stay in check. Work AI-native. Lead with specs, then hand agents end-to-end tasks, from exploring source data to building models, tests, and documentation. Let agents run loose in the wild (with some guardrails in place). You hold agent and human work to the same review bar, so code from Claude and code from a teammate get the same scrutiny. Share what you learn, and help set the playbook for agentic data work. What We Look For: You have 3+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI development, building data products people rely on. You write strong SQL and have built and maintained dbt models in production. You’ve worked in a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. You’ve worked with ELT ingestion tools like Fivetran and can troubleshoot source-data issues such as schema changes, late-arriving data, and API limits. You understand data modeling: dimensional models, medallion layering, and clear reasoning about grain, slowly changing dimensions, and event lifecycles. You’ve built dashboards or self-service data products that people use to make decisions. You test and document your work as a habit. You’re curious about the business. You ask what decision a request supports before you start building. You use AI agents for real multi-step work, like writing SQL and dbt models, generating tests, and drafting documentation, and you verify what they produce. You explain your work clearly to technical and non-technical partners. You take ownership. You see work through, ask for help when you’re stuck, and look for ways to make things better. Bonus Points You’ve evaluated LLM or natural-language analytics output, for example with golden sets or regression testing. You’ve worked in hospitality, events, real estate, or another customer-centric, multi-location business. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. Job duties and responsibilities are subject to change based on changing business needs and conditions. Salary Min: $120,000 Salary Max: $160,000 This role is also eligible for Convene's annual incentive performance bonus plan. This information reflects the anticipated base salary range for this position based on current national data. Minimums and maximums may vary based on location. Individual pay is based on skills, experience and other relevant factors. We’re Here For You: At Convene Hospitality Group, we want you to feel supported in every part of your life. Here’s what you can expect: Health & Wellness: Day-one health coverage for you and your family, 24/7 virtual care, emotional well-being support, and fertility & family planning benefits. Because your well-being matters, inside and outside of work. Time Off & Balance: Generous PTO, your birthday off (because, of course!), paid parental leave, and a year-end holiday closure to recharge. Financial Growth: 401K with company match and support for education, courses, and certifications. We invest in you so you can grow personally and professionally. Development & Recognition: Ongoing career growth opportunities plus recognition programs to celebrate milestones. jobs.jd: (ID: 2026-3889) Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Benefits We Offer: 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays 401K match up to 5% Educational Benefits for Career Growth Employee Referral Bonus Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN) Position Overview The Bioinformatics Fellow for Multi-Omics Analysis will conduct comprehensive analyses of multi-omics data generated from organoid systems and corresponding normal tissues. The incumbent will characterize organoid fidelity, identify biomarkers of successful differentiation, and develop computational frameworks for organoid quality assessment, while gaining substantive training in integrative analysis of single-cell and multi-omics data. The work is central to the SOM Center’s research objectives, and the position is intended to prepare the Fellow for an independent research career in academia, government, or industry. Key Responsibilities Multi-omics analysis. Analyze complex datasets including single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, and metabolomics data from a range of organoid systems and their tissue counterparts. Pipeline development. Develop and implement computational pipelines for data processing, quality control, and statistical analysis, and document them so that analyses are reproducible across the Center. Benchmarking. Integrate SOM-generated data with publicly available datasets in order to benchmark organoid characteristics against normal tissue profiles. Method development. Develop and refine analytical approaches — including machine learning methods where appropriate — for classifying cellular states and assessing organoid quality, and contribute to standardized assessment protocols. Collaboration and interpretation. Work closely with experimental teams to interpret results and guide protocol optimization, and collaborate with other computational staff on cross-modality data integration. Dissemination. Contribute to manuscript preparation and present findings at scientific conferences. Required Qualifications Education. Doctoral degree (PhD) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biostatistics, or a related quantitative field, completed or anticipated prior to the start of the appointment. Single-cell analysis. Extensive experience with single-cell data analysis, including familiarity with tools such as Seurat, Scanpy, or comparable platforms. Programming. Strong programming proficiency in R and Python, together with experience in statistical analysis and data visualization. Omics workflows. Working knowledge of proteomics and metabolomics data analysis workflows. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience analyzing organoid datasets. Experience with machine learning approaches for biological data, familiarity with pathway analysis tools, and knowledge of developmental biology principles. Experience with high-performance computing environments and version control systems. jobs.jd:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


ROLE OVERVIEW:

We're growing our Canadian Public Sector Delivery team and hiring Public Sector Delivery Analysts to help run some of the most consequential AI deployments in the country. You'll work alongside our Engineering Program Managers (EPMs), Technical Leads, and senior leadership to keep large, multi-stakeholder government programs organized, documented, and moving.

This is a hands-on delivery role for individuals who want exposure to enterprise AI and high-stakes program delivery while taking pride in making complex programs run smoothly. As a member of our small, senior team, you'll deliver sovereign AI to the Government of Canada, engage directly with clients from day one on a clear path toward leading engagements, and learn how frontier AI products are deployed in real, high-security environments.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Drive things to closure. Partner with the EPM and Technical Leads to track actions, dependencies, and blockers across Cohere and client teams making sure nothing slips.

 - Show up in front of the client. Prepare and coordinate client sessions, capture outcomes, and progressively lead working-level sessions such as use-case and story refinement.

 - Run the cadence. Own the meeting and reporting rhythm including agendas, scheduling, minutes, and follow-ups so every forum lands on time with clear next steps.

 - Own the delivery artefacts. Build and maintain the plans, status reports, RAID logs, decision records, use-case registers, and traceability documentation that keep our engagements audit-ready and our clients confident.

 - Keep the record straight. Maintain a single source of truth for program documentation in our public sector document management environment.
   


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 1–4 years of experience in technology or management consulting, professional services, or an in-house technical delivery team.

 - Delivery discipline. You've run RAID, action, and decision logs, refined user stories, maintained project plans on real projects and kept them accurate and clear.

 - Client presence. You can lead a working session in front of a client, read the room, and know what to say and what to hold.

 - Strong written communication. You think through the message before you build the slide. Advanced PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 - Technical fluency. You're comfortable discussing APIs, integrations, environments, testing, and releases. You can talk with engineers and report back accurately.

 - Follow-through. You close items without a second reminder and know what to escalate and when.

 - Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance.

 - Based in the Ottawa area.

 - University Degree in Business/Commerce, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering or similar preferred.

 - Nice-to-have: High degree of French language proficiency.
   


WORKING LOCATION:

This role is hybrid with the requirement to be based out of Ottawa - note, there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement.

This role requires eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and a high degree of French language proficiency is a nice-to-have.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

jobs.title: LN Concerts, Social Insights Analyst
jobs.jd: Job Summary: WHO ARE WE? Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com . WHO ARE YOU? Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! THE JOB The Social Insights Analyst will play a key role in Live Nation Entertainment’s Concert division, living and breathing in social listening, reporting and analytics from start to finish, including query building, dashboard development and delivering reports. This role will uncover insights and trends for actionable storytelling opportunities, guide marketing strategy, and inform cross-functional partners on social, cultural, and influencer trends. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Analytics & Strategy, this position is ideal for someone who thrives in building scalable analytics systems while staying deeply connected to cultural and platform trends and developments. We're looking for a data-minded storyteller who lives at the intersection of social media and analytics. You'll own reporting and measurement for earned conversation tied to tours, on-sales, and artist activations. This is a great fit for someone who's equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and a comment section. WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO Own measurement and analysis of earned social conversation: mentions, share of voice, sentiment, engagement on non-owned posts, organic reach, and virality across Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, and emerging platforms. Run social listening across tour cycles (from announcements, on-sales to live moments), tracking fan sentiment, conversation volume, and flagging shifts in real time. Measure fan- and creator-generated content (UGC): what's made, how it spreads, which moments drive organic amplification, and how artists, media, and fan accounts pick it up. Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports (daily, weekly, campaign-level, ad-hoc, and post-mortem), using Boolean logic to sharpen queries and insights delivery. Run competitive and benchmark analysis to contextualize our performance. Build alert systems for emerging artist topics, trends, and brand risks, supporting Community Management, Marketing, and PR/Comms in shaping response messaging. Partner with social listening-tool vendors and cross-functional teams to improve benchmarks, KPIs, alerts, and depth of insight. Uncover fan insights through audience demographics to help guide campaign planning WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING 2–4 years in social media analytics, social listening, and/or digital insights with a focus on earned measurement (agency or in-house social team preferred). Hands-on experience with social listening and publishing tools (Meltwater, Brandwatch, Sprout, Quid, etc.) plus platform-native analytics. Comfortable with audience demographic tools such as Audiense as well as platform follower demographics through CreatorIQ. Fluency in earned-social metrics (share of voice, sentiment, mention volume) and a clear sense of which ones actually matter. Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and a solid grasp of Boolean logic for query development. Proven ability to own analytics end-to-end (query design, reporting, dashboard development and maintenance), with a track record of spotting and fixing gaps in reporting infrastructure. Deep understanding of social platforms as both a fan and an analyst: how conversation forms, why things spread, what fans respond to, plus genuine curiosity about cultural trends, emerging formats, and creator marketing. Strong communication skills: you can turn a spike in conversation into a one-slide "so what" for non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented, organized, and able to juggle multiple projects and deadlines under pressure. A proactive, collaborative team player who flags insights before they're asked for and adapts to evolving leadership needs. Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Analytics, or a related field. NICE TO HAVE: Passion for live music, touring, and artist marketing. Experience with sentiment analysis, text/topic classification, or unstructured conversation data. Familiarity with creator/influencer earned-coverage measurement. Experience connecting earned social signals to broader marketing or fan-growth outcomes. jobs.title: Market Analyst
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

jobs.jd:
The Core Data Science team builds the products and data assets that let teams across Zoox measure and improve the autonomy and operational performance of our fleet. You’ll piece together the constituent components into a coherent, easy-to-use simulation environment, filling in the gaps, and building generalizable mechanisms so data scientists can measure their algorithm's impact on fleet efficiency. You'll join a diverse, experienced team with rapidly growing scope while working with one of the industry's most valuable autonomous vehicle datasets.
 Design, prototype, and help deploy algorithms for vehicle assignment, staging, routing, and pricing Model the inputs to orchestration (rider demand, data-collection value, servicing needs, events, and policies) as objectives and constraints Work with specialists in marketplace economics, forecasting, and autonomy to turn their models into decisions the fleet acts on Measure impact on revenue, utilization, and rider experience through simulation, offline evaluation, and online experiments Contribute to how we evaluate and roll out orchestration improvements PhD or MS with 2+ years of relevant industry or research experience, in operations research, robotics, controls, transportation, computer science, applied math, or a related field Deep expertise in at least one of: combinatorial/integer optimization, stochastic optimization or control, reinforcement learning/approximate DP, network flows, or marketplace/demand modeling, plus the curiosity to work across the rest Strong coding skills in Python, C++, or Rust; you write clean, tested, version-controlled code Ability to turn ambiguous real-world problems into well-defined models and explain the tradeoffs to non-specialists Good communication and collaboration skills Internship or research experience in ride-hailing, delivery, logistics, or AV fleets (dispatch, routing, rebalancing, pricing) Algorithms deployed in production or used on real operational data Publications in operations research, transportation, or robotics venues About Zoox

jobs.jd:
ABOUT GEN:

Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.

At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.

If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen.




ROLE OVERVIEW

The Marketing Analyst – Network Optimization will use data and experimentation to uncover what drives marketplace performance, turning analysis into clear, actionable recommendations that shape the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of tests. This role sits at the intersection of marketing analytics, data science, product, and commercial strategy.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, moving quickly from questions to analysis to action. At the core of the role: translating business questions into testable hypotheses, designing sound experiments, monitoring live tests, and delivering clear, data-driven readouts that inform optimization decisions — supported by day-to-day management of the test agenda.



Key Responsibilities

Marketplace and Marketing Analytics

 - Conduct exploratory analysis to understand changes in customer behavior, traffic quality, offer engagement, and downstream outcomes.

 - Monitor marketplace and funnel performance to identify optimization opportunities across customer experience, offer display, partner performance, and monetization.

 - Support opportunity sizing and business-case development for proposed optimization initiatives.

 - Partner with analytics and data science teams to improve measurement quality, data reliability, and experimentation velocity.

 - Help develop repeatable processes for rapid testing, post-test analysis, and continuous optimization.

Test Design and Execution

 - Translate business opportunities and performance signals into clear hypotheses, test objectives, target populations, success metrics, and guardrail metrics.

 - Coordinate test setup, launch readiness, audience splits, documentation, timelines, and stakeholder communication.

 - Work quickly and pragmatically while maintaining analytical rigor and attention to detail.

Test Readouts and Reporting

 - Analyze metrics such as impressions, click-through rate, conversion, click-to-funded rate, revenue, revenue per lead, revenue per click, and partner or network efficiency.

 - Identify meaningful changes, anomalies, and emerging opportunities that require investigation or follow-up testing.

 - Build and maintain recurring reports, dashboards, and scorecards for the test pipeline, experiment status, and business impact.

 - Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including marketing, product, finance, operations, and leadership.

 - Maintain consistent standards for experiment documentation, naming, tracking, and knowledge sharing.

 - Capture and distribute learnings so that successful approaches can be scaled and unsuccessful approaches can inform future tests.

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in marketing analytics, statistics, economics, business, mathematics, computer science, or a related quantitative field.

 - 1–3 years of experience in marketing analytics, product analytics, growth analytics, experimentation, revenue analytics, or a related discipline.

 - Experience working with A/B tests, holdout tests, campaign measurement, or other forms of controlled experimentation.

 - Strong analytical skills and proficiency with SQL or Python, Excel, or a comparable data analysis tool.

 - Ability to create clear reports, dashboards, presentations, and written test readouts.

 - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and cross-functional environment.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Familiarity with marketplace, lending, advertising, e-commerce, lead-generation, or other two-sided platform businesses.

 - Exposure to funnel analysis, offer ranking, pricing, partner optimization, customer segmentation, or revenue optimization.

 - Experience coordinating cross-functional projects or maintaining a structured test backlog.

 - Experience presenting analytical findings and recommendations to business stakeholders.

What Success Looks Like

 - Tests are well documented, launched on schedule, and aligned to clearly defined business questions.

 - Stakeholders have an accurate, up-to-date view of the test agenda, status, owners, dependencies, and next steps.

 - Test readouts are timely, accurate, and easy to understand.

 - Reporting helps teams identify performance changes, prioritize opportunities, and make faster decisions.

 - Experiment learnings are consistently shared and translated into follow-up actions or scalable optimization opportunities.

 - The team increases test velocity while maintaining sound measurement and decision quality.

Working Style

 - Takes ownership, follows through, and proactively communicates risks or blockers.

 - Enjoys learning in a dynamic environment with changing priorities.

jobs.jd:
For this role on the Mail team, Superhuman offers a remote-flexible work model, whereas other Data Science roles may be aligned with a specific hub based on business needs. This gives team members plenty of focus time and the flexibility to do their best work wherever they're based, while staying closely connected to a collaborative, tight-knit team culture. A hybrid setup is available for those based in San Francisco, New York City, or Seattle.




ABOUT SUPERHUMAN

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company's products include Grammarly's writing assistance, Docs’ collaborative workspace, Mail's inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and automatically delivers help. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com http://superhuman.com and about our values here https://superhuman.com/company/values.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Want to use data science to shape how one of the most beloved productivity products in the world grows, retains, and delights its users? This Data Scientist position is embedded in the Superhuman Mail https://superhuman.com/mail business unit, working alongside Data Engineering, Finance, RevOps, and UX Market Research. Together, you act as one numbers-and-insights team, with a direct line to the leaders setting strategy and a shared mandate to move the metrics that matter.



Superhuman Mail is the fastest, most AI-native email experience ever built. It helps knowledge workers and teams fly through their inbox twice as fast, stay on top of what matters most, and collaborate without friction — saving users four hours every single week. Where email has barely changed in decades, Superhuman Mail is reimagining it from the ground up: AI that drafts replies in your voice, auto-labels and triages incoming messages, surfaces follow-ups before you drop the ball, and can even send emails on your behalf. It serves everyone, from individual professionals to Fortune 500 sales teams, and boasts a deeply loyal user base and a product people genuinely love. The data environment is rich, the growth questions are hard, and the opportunity to drive real impact — on acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion — is enormous.



Your work on Mail is part of a broader platform story. The Superhuman Platform suite includes Grammarly's writing assistance, Mail, Docs, Databases, and Go, our proactive AI assistant. As a compound startup, we're building an integrated suite rather than separate tools — so insights you surface in Mail ripple across the full product portfolio, and cross-product growth loops connect the dots between how users discover, adopt, and expand across the suite. Our products serve both consumers and enterprises, creating an unusually rich data environment. Our user base spans students and knowledge workers, individual users and Fortune 500 companies, universities and global enterprises, across a growing range of languages and markets. That breadth creates no shortage of important questions to own.



This is an opportunity for those drawn to complex, high-stakes growth problems — in a product people are passionate about — who want their work to measurably change outcomes.



What you’ll do

 - Be the embedded data science partner for the Mail core product team — shaping feature strategy, prioritization, and roadmap decisions with evidence, not just fielding ad hoc requests.

 - Define and own the metrics that matter for Mail: activation milestones, engagement depth, retention curves, and the leading indicators that tell us whether a new feature is actually changing how people work in their inbox.

 - Design and run experiments across the Mail product lifecycle — from onboarding and first-week activation to long-term habit formation — and build the measurement frameworks that separate signal from noise.

 - Shape the measurement strategy for Mail's AI features — Auto Drafts, Auto Labels, Auto Archive, Calendar, MCP, and the agentic capabilities on the roadmap — by defining quality frameworks and behavioral metrics that show whether AI is making users genuinely faster and more effective.

 - Figure out what makes Mail sticky: which features drive the deepest engagement, what the activation sequence looks like for users who become power users, and where in the funnel we're leaving value on the table.

 - Partner with product-led and sales-led growth to identify and quantify the levers that turn individual users into team expansions — and surface the product signals that predict conversion and churn.

 - Use data to craft remarkable product moments — turning behavioral insight into smarter onboarding flows, better feature discovery, and engagement nudges that feel natural rather than forced. This includes understanding how features such as Calendar scheduling and MCP-driven workflows change the way users interact with Mail on a day-to-day basis.

 - Communicate findings clearly to PMs, designers, engineers, and executives — from experiment readouts to strategic deep-dives — and help raise the bar on how the Mail team makes decisions with data.

You'll do this alongside product managers, engineers, designers, and ML engineers, and in close partnership with our Experimentation team (running on Statsig), whose platform lets us ship, test, and learn quickly. We think from first principles and stay with the hardest product problems through the messy middle. Mail is a product people are genuinely passionate about — the questions are hard, the feedback loop is fast, and the opportunity to shape how millions of people experience their inbox is real.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - You have 7+ years of data science experience and a track record of driving measurable impact for business and customers.

 - You have deep expertise in experimentation and causal inference. You’re fluent in A/B testing as well as quasi-experimental and observational methods, and you know when to use each.

 - You’re fluent in Python and SQL, with strong data exploration and manipulation skills.

 - You have strong applied statistics skills and machine learning skills, and you use them to drive product and growth decisions.

 - You can translate ambiguous business questions into sound experimental designs, measurement plans, and metrics.

 - You influence cross-functional partners and turn technical insight into action through clear communication, empathetic building, and openness to ideas from anywhere.

 - You’re a self-starting, creative problem-solver who distills problems to their core and thrives with ambiguity.

 - You have a bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, data science, or a similar field); an advanced degree or equivalent practical experience is preferred.


NICE TO HAVE

 - You have experience working at a fast-growing startup, on AI-native consumer products, and/or in B2B/SaaS.

 - You’ve been a strategic thought partner to product, growth, or business leaders, driving data-driven decisions.

 - You’ve evaluated the quality of AI, LLM, or agentic products hands-on.

 - You’re comfortable using AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code or Codex to move faster, and you have the judgment to validate and supervise their output.

 - You’re familiar with experimentation platforms such as Statsig and modern data stacks such as Databricks.

 - You have experience with product-led growth and/or lifecycle and marketing analytics.

 - You’ve helped data science teams establish the methods, standards, and processes they use to collaborate.

jobs.title: Quantitative Scientist, Forecasting & Demand Planning
jobs.jd: Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team. Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder. Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France. As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process. We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have. We're looking for a Quantitative Scientist, Forecasting & Demand Planning to help build the quantitative modeling capability at the core of Collectors' next phase of growth. This is unlike almost any other quantitative role in fintech or financial services. You'll be modeling asset classes — vintage sports cards, rare coins, sealed video games — where the data is uniquely ours, the domain expertise lives in-house, and the opportunity to build something from first principles is wide open. You'll join a small, early-stage team and work directly with its leader on modeling and infrastructure. We're looking for someone who wants to ship real models and grow quickly alongside the function. What You'll Do Modeling & Production: Leverage Collectors' proprietary grading, authentication, search and transaction data — one of the deepest datasets in the collectibles industry — as a core modeling advantage Partner with Engineering to deploy models into production systems with appropriate monitoring, explainability, and feedback loops Continuously improve model performance using new data sources, features, and methodologies Partner with other members of the Product & Technology team to validate valuation models through rigorous backtesting and experimentation. Collaborate with domain experts to improve feature engineering to ensure our models reflect the market nuances that drive sale prices Financial Forecasting: Build quantitative models that forecast market dynamics, asset valuations, and pricing trends across collectible categories (cards, coins, comics, banknotes, games, and beyond) Develop and refine intelligence that supports and enhances our grading and authentication businesses Generate insights that inform product, pricing, and go-to-market strategy across the Collectors portfolio Team & Collaboration: Join the Quantitative Sciences function as one of its first members, working directly with its leader Contribute to the team's roadmap, research agenda, and technical standards Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Operations to understand business needs and turn them into well-scoped modeling work. Who You Are 3–5 years of experience in quantitative finance, data science, machine learning, or a related field, with hands-on experience in pricing, demand forecasting, or asset valuation Solid ML fundamentals — you’ve built and validated supervised models on real data and have helped get at least one into production, not just in notebooks Strong Python and SQL — you’re fluent with the standard data stack (pandas, scikit-learn or similar) and comfortable working directly with large datasets Financial modeling foundations — you're familiar with concepts like time series forecasting, scenario analysis, and asset pricing Forecasting experience — you’ve built time series or demand forecasts and can produce scenario ranges (downside, base, upside), not just point estimates Production mindset — you care about model reliability, monitoring, drift detection, and working closely with engineering teams Comfort with ambiguity — you can make progress in a fast-moving environment and are comfortable working on problems with limited precedent Ownership and follow-through — you can take a loosely defined problem, scope it, and carry it to a shipped result with guidance from your lead Clear communication — you can explain your models and results to non-technical partners and back your recommendations with data Intellectual curiosity about alternative assets — you're excited (not intimidated) by the prospect of modeling asset classes that don't have decades of structured financial data behind them Nice to Haves Experience in fintech or alternative/exotic asset valuation Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a quantitative discipline — statistics, applied math, CS, physics, economics, operations research, or similar Exposure to demand planning or capacity planning in an operations-heavy business Personal interest in collectibles, trading cards, coins, or related hobbyist markets (not required, but it helps) Why This Role Proprietary data. Collectors has authenticated and graded hundreds of millions of collectibles. You'll build models on top of a dataset that simply doesn't exist anywhere else. Early-stage team. You'll join the Quantitative Sciences function near its start and help shape the models, the roadmap, and the culture. Tangible business impact. The models you build will directly power how we price, plan capacity, and grow across a rapidly expanding market. Category-defining work. Collectibles are becoming a recognized asset class. You'll help build the quantitative infrastructure that makes that possible. Room to grow. You’ll work directly with the function’s leader, get hands-on coaching, and take on more scope as the team and the models mature. Compensation & Benefits The estimated salary for this role is $187,400 - $253,500. Actual compensation may vary based on relevant experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other role-specific factors. Reasons To Join Us Health Insurance: All full-time employees are eligible to enroll in Medical, Dental, and Vision 401(K) Matching Plan: We are proud to offer a competitive 401k matching plan to our employees to support their future financial goals Vacation: All full-time employees are eligible for paid vacation Holiday Pay: All regular, full-time employees are eligible for ten company-paid holidays Employee Discounts: Employees receive discounts on select grading services for different segments Flexible Hours: Many of our teams offer flexible schedules with varying shifts and work-from-home opportunities Fun Working Environment: Our team members are invited to company-wide events, celebrations, and department outings Collectors uses e-Verify to validate your ability to work legally in the United States. We are aware that there are instances where individuals are receiving job offers that fraudulently allege to be from Collectors or one of our business units. This type of fraud can be carried out through false websites, through fake e-mails claiming to be from the company or through social media. We never ask for personal information such as your bank account, Social Security numbers or National IDs, nor do we send or request payments for the purchase of business-related equipment. We are the region's locally headquartered bank and wealth management company. We are honored to consistently be named a Top Workplace by our Associates, who make a difference every day for the people, businesses, and Communities we serve. We Stand For Service® is more than part of our name, it’s our mission and our purpose. As a Cash Connect Compliance Operations Analyst, you'll play a critical role in supporting regulatory compliance, operational risk management, and process improvement initiatives across Cash Connect operations. You'll partner with Compliance, Operations, Technology, and external vendors to enhance reporting accuracy, strengthen internal controls, support audit readiness, and drive operational excellence across the organization. This role provides the opportunity to leverage banking operations and compliance experience while gaining broader exposure to enterprise risk management, regulatory oversight, and cross-functional process improvement initiatives. Job Responsibilities: Support Cash Connect regulatory compliance activities, including Currency Transaction Reporting (CTR), customer due diligence, and related reporting requirements. Monitor compliance, operational, and risk metrics to identify trends, reporting exceptions, and opportunities to strengthen controls and improve processes. Investigate and resolve reporting, system, and data-quality issues by partnering with Compliance, Operations, Technology, and other business stakeholders. Prepare reporting, dashboards, and analysis to support regulatory compliance, risk management, and business decision-making. Participate in system enhancements, testing, process improvements, and regulatory change initiatives to drive operational efficiency and reporting accuracy. Coordinate audit-related activities, including regulatory examinations, internal audits, vendor oversight reviews, and remediation efforts. Support insurance compliance, claims administration, loss reporting, and related risk-management activities. Maintain policies, procedures, documentation, and records to ensure compliance with regulatory, audit, and operational requirements. Collaborate across teams and contribute to special projects, onboarding activities, and other initiatives that support Cash Connect operations and risk management. Support additional projects and initiatives that contribute to the success of the Cash Connect team and broader organization. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in a related field preferred and 2+ years of experience in banking operations, compliance, branch leadership, risk management, regulatory reporting, audit, financial services, or a related function. Working knowledge of banking regulations, BSA/AML requirements, Currency Transaction Reporting (CTR), operational controls, and compliance-related processes. jobs.title: Quantitative Analyst
jobs.jd: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description Quantitative Analyst, Municipal Fixed Income Your Team The Quantitative Analyst will be part of the broader quantitative team supporting Invesco Fixed Income. The team develops market research, data, models, and analytical tools that strengthen investment decision-making, portfolio construction, and risk management. This role will focus on municipal strategies and work closely with portfolio managers and credit researchers on market, portfolio, and security-level questions. The analyst will also partner with quantitative, technology, and data colleagues to build reliable data and reusable analytical capabilities. Your Role As a Quantitative Analyst, you will combine municipal market knowledge, quantitative analysis, and practical implementation to support portfolio managers and credit researchers. You will identify and evaluate investment questions involving relative value, portfolio positioning, risk, performance, and market structure and build the tools needed to test and apply your ideas. You will have end-to-end responsibility for the municipal data supporting this work, from understanding source systems and resolving discrepancies to producing controlled analytical datasets. The role requires curiosity about markets and an interest in the daily work of turning data and investment ideas into reliable, useful analytics. You Will Be Responsible For: Generating and evaluating quantitative investment ideas related to municipal relative value, portfolio positioning, performance drivers, and market opportunities. Measuring portfolio exposures on an absolute and benchmark-relative basis, including interest-rate, yield-curve, spread, credit, liquidity, and optionality risks. Developing scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess how market changes could affect performance, volatility, distributions, and portfolio positioning. Investigating differences between expected and realized performance, distinguishing market and economic drivers from data or model issues, and communicating findings to portfolio managers and credit researchers. Evaluating leverage and funding risks, including tender option bond and variable-rate municipal term preferred exposures and their implications for total return, liquidity, and distributions. Managing municipal data end to end, including acquisition, definitions, transformations, timing, lineage, quality controls, reconciliation, and availability across systems such as Perform and Aladdin. Building and maintaining analytical tools and automated workflows for holdings, transactions, pricing, benchmarks, risk, and performance while reducing routine manual processing. Partnering with investment, quantitative, technology, and data colleagues to test new ideas, implement useful analytics, and contribute reusable data, methods, and code to the broader platform. The Experience You Bring: Experience applying quantitative analysis to fixed-income markets, relative value, portfolio risk, performance attribution, or portfolio construction. Knowledge of municipal securities, market conventions, portfolio structures, benchmarks, and sources of risk, or relevant fixed-income experience and a demonstrated ability to develop new market expertise. Demonstrated ability to formulate investment or analytical questions and build practical tools, models, or applications to evaluate them. Strong hands-on Python and SQL skills, including experience working with complex datasets and automating analytical workflows. Experience investigating data from multiple systems, reconciling inconsistencies, establishing data-quality controls, and developing reliable analytical datasets. Familiarity with modern development practices and platforms such as Git or GitHub, cloud infrastructure, Snowflake, Databricks, or comparable technologies. Experience using AI-assisted research or development tools to explore ideas, develop code, test analytical approaches, or improve productivity. Strong judgment and communication skills, including the ability to connect technical analysis to market developments, portfolio exposures, and practical investment decisions. The salary range for this position in New York City is 145,000 - 158,000 USD/year. The total compensation offered for this position includes salary and incentive pay and will vary based on skills, experience and location Full Time / Part Time Full time Worker Type Employee Job Exempt (Yes / No) Yes Workplace Model Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development. jobs.title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
jobs.jd:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

 - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

 - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

 - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

 - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

 - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

 - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

 - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

jobs.title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI
jobs.jd:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.


MERCOR AI RESEARCH FUND GRANTS: ECONOMICS OF AI

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897), and our funding of benchmarking research.

The grant supports:

 - The time of experts from Mercor's platform

 - Researcher hours

 - API costs

 - Stipends for event and conference attendance


BUDGET CATEGORIES

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

 - Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

 - Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

 - Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.



 


RESEARCH AGENDA

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor

 - How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task?

 - To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes?

 - What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)?

 - How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement?



2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity

 - How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive?

 - What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions?

 - How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work?

 - Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume?



3. Enterprise adoption and returns

 - What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate?

 - How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing?

 - How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation?

 - What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains?



 


ELIGIBILITY

 

 - Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

 - Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom

We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

 


TIMELINE

 

 - Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)

 - Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.

 
 


HOW TO APPLY

We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:

 - Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

 - Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

 - Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

 - Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

 - Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

 - Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

 - Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).
   
   - Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget




GUIDANCE FOR APPLICANTS.

 - Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

 - The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

 - Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

 - Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

 
 


AWARD TERMS

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

The College teaches undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students on campus and online in more than 90 programs. jobs.title: Data Ops - Data Builder
jobs.jd: This Data Management Strategy & Governance Advisor , offers an exciting opportunity to build on your strengths, expand your impact, and continue growing within the organization. Job Description The Data Builder is the hands-on builder responsible for turning architectural design and business requirements into trusted, reusable data products through MVP that are production grade. Reporting to the Senior Director, Data Operations & Data Management, this role builds to the enterprise-agnostic Silver foundation designed by Data Architecture and co-designs and builds Gold data products where business logic, metrics, and functional knowledge live. This is a hands-on individual contributor role — the build authority that blends business fluency and data engineering discipline in equal measure , authoring Gold data products that answer the question the first time and building them to production standard. This role is a critical execution counterpart to Data Architecture and Data Analysis, Products & Integration , building faithfully against their designs and requirements and compressing the path from new data to a production-grade, reusable asset. It is an exciting opportunity to join the team transforming how Cigna builds and reuses data — delivered through MVP. Key Responsibilities Rapid Build & Delivery Build architecture’s designs and analysis’s requirements into production-ready solutions through MVP. Work new and unfamiliar data quickly into a working solution that answers the business question at hand. Refactor learning-stage and bespoke work into durable, reusable, production-ready assets. Silver — Build to Architecture’s Design Build the physical Silver structures to the enterprise-agnostic Silver model and reference patterns designed by Data Architecture. Implement the design faithfully and promote it to production through governed CI/CD pipelines . Capture business context and metadata at build, and hand off to trusted partner teams as readiness allows. Gold — Democratized, Delivered Through MVP Treat the Gold layer as democratized — Data Operations may own specific Gold assets and assists other teams in building theirs. Deliver Gold solutions through build-through-MVP , promoted to production-grade through governed CI/CD pipelines regardless of owner. Uphold the build standards and guardrails any Gold solution must meet, so a federated Gold layer stays stable and production-grade across owning teams. Engineering Discipline & Production Readiness Build to production standards from day one so the lift from MVP to production is simple, not a rebuild. Apply consistent development patterns, naming conventions, and build standards with specific focus on the connectivity across all data products to create a more connected data ecosystem. Move work through the CI/CD pipeline — develop, test, and productionize — clearing quality, security, and cost checks on first pass. Apply AI and automation to accelerate build and testing without bypassing governance, security, or quality expectations. Partnership & Collaboration Partner with Data Architecture — building to their Silver design and co-designing Gold within the standards they set. Partner with Data Analysis, Products & Integration — who bring the requirements, business rules, and acceptance criteria this role builds against. Partner with Platform Engineering / IT and DevOps & AI Enablement — who own ingestion, pipelines, and the automation frameworks this role builds on. Partner with data science and business analytics teams so Gold data products serve their models, analyses, and decisions. Set the design and hold Data Operations standards across the Hyderabad Data Operations team and outside service partners as part of a global delivery model. What This Role Is Not Not a pure data engineering or platform role. Not the owner of the enterprise Silver model. Not the primary business-engagement or requirements role. Not the owner of the Gold layer, which is democratized across teams. Not a governance policy, stewardship, or BI reporting role. This role exists to build real data solutions that get used — designed for the business, engineered to last, delivered through MVP. Required Experience & Capabilities 3+ years building production-grade data solutions , with demonstrated depth in analytics engineering or equivalent business-plus-build work. A genuine 50/50 blend of business fluency and hands-on engineering discipline . Hands-on experience with Databricks, Spark, Unity Catalog, SQL, and Python . Familiarity with Snowflake and Teradata in addition to a Databricks-first stack. Expert knowledge of dimensional and medallion (Silver / Gold) modeling within an enterprise-agnostic data model. Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, automated code evaluation, and controlled promotion to production. Strong software-engineering discipline — version control (Git), code review, and efficient, reusable code. Performance-tuning and cost-optimizing Spark and SQL transformations at scale. Familiarity with data governance and cataloging tooling such as Collibra. Automated data-quality testing and validation built into every solution. Demonstrated ability to learn a new data domain fast and turn business logic into reusable data products. Demonstrated ability to apply AI and automation to accelerate build while preserving quality and governance. Experience in complex, regulated enterprises preferred; healthcare or PBM data a plus. Measures of Success New data reaches a trusted, production-grade asset in a short cycle time If you will be working at home occasionally or permanently, the internet connection must be obtained through a cable broadband or fiber optic internet service provider with speeds of at least 10Mbps download/5Mbps upload. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary of 102,400 - 170,600 USD / yearly, depending on relevant factors, including experience and geographic location. This role is also anticipated to be eligible to participate in an annual bonus plan. At The Cigna Group, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive range of benefits, with a focus on supporting your whole health. Starting on day one of your employment, you’ll be offered several health-related benefits including medical, vision, dental, and well-being and behavioral health programs. We also offer 401(k), company paid life insurance, tuition reimbursement, a minimum of 18 days of paid time off per year, paid holidays, and leaves of absence. At The Cigna Group, we’re dedicated to improving the health and vitality of those we serve. Through our divisions Cigna Healthcare and Evernorth Health Services, we are committed to enhancing the lives of our clients, customers and patients. Join us in driving growth and improving lives.
